attributes.description: Indicates whether this allocation is part of a dollar cost averaging program where premium is systematically transferred from a fixed account to investment funds over time.

attributes.description: Minimum guaranteed interest rate for this fund allocation, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 0.00 for 0% floor). Protects against negative index performance in IUL and FIA products.

attributes.name: fund_risk_rating
attributes.description: Risk profile classification of the investment fund used for suitability assessment and portfolio construction.

attributes.name: index_segment_end_date
attributes.description: For IUL and FIA products, the end date of the current index crediting segment or term when index gains/losses are calculated and credited.

attributes.name: index_segment_start_date

attributes.name: index_segment_term_years

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: last_rebalance_date
attributes.description: Date when the most recent automatic or manual rebalancing of account value to target allocation percentages was executed.

attributes.name: maximum_allocation_percentage
attributes.description: Maximum percentage that can be allocated to this fund per product rules or regulatory requirements. Used for compliance validation during allocation changes.

attributes.name: minimum_allocation_percentage
attributes.description: Minimum percentage that must be maintained in this fund per product rules or regulatory requirements. Used for compliance validation during allocation changes.

attributes.name: mortality_and_expense_risk_charge

attributes.name: rebalancing_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the policy account value is automatically rebalanced to match the target allocation percentages. 'none' indicates no automatic rebalancing.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the policy administration system or platform that originated this allocation record (e.g., FAST, SAPIENS, ORACLE_IPAS).

attributes.name: spread_rate
attributes.description: Percentage deducted from index gains before crediting to the policy account value, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 2.50 for 2.5% spread). Alternative to cap rate in some indexed product designs.

products.name: service_request
products.description: SSOT for all post-issue policy servicing transactions, contractual endorsements, administrative changes, policy conversions, and IRC Section 1035 tax-free exchanges processed through the Policy Administration System. Encompasses administrative service requests, formal contractual amendments (endorsements), term-to-permanent conversions, and 1035 exchange transactions. Captures request/endorsement type (address change, beneficiary change, ownership change, premium mode change, face amount change, dividend option change, name change, duplicate policy contract request, rider addition/removal, collateral assignment, reinstatement, conversion, 1035 exchange), endorsement number (for contractual amendments), amendment effective date, request channel (phone, web portal, agent, mail), request date, effective date, request status (received, in-review, completed, NIGO — Not In Good Order, cancelled), prior value, new value, reason code, NIGO reason code, SLA due date, completion date, processing agent ID, source system transaction ID. For conversions: source policy type (YRT, term), target policy type (WL, UL, IUL), conversion credit amount, conversion privilege expiry date, evidence of insurability waived flag, new policy reference. For 1035 exchanges: exchange type (life-to-life, annuity-to-annuity, life-to-annuity), surrendering carrier name, surrendering policy number, exchange amount transferred, cost basis transferred, gain deferred, IRS Form 1035 attestation flag. Provides full audit trail of all contractual modifications. Supports policy servicing SLA monitoring, NIGO reduction initiatives, and regulatory audit trail requirements.

products.name: risk_assessment
products.description: Comprehensive underwriting risk evaluation master record for a life or annuity application, encompassing medical, financial, and compliance risk dimensions in a single holistic assessment. Medical underwriting: captures mortality and morbidity risk classification outputs, build chart results, aviation/avocation hazard ratings, APS review outcomes, MIB inquiry findings, and overall medical risk score. Financial underwriting: captures insurable interest determination, income replacement multiple analysis, human life value (HLV) calculation, business insurance justification (key person, buy-sell), existing coverage in-force summary, financial statement review notes, and financial underwriting decision outcome — ensures coverage amounts are financially justified and detects potential over-insurance. STOLI/IOLI detection: captures STOLI indicator flags (premium financing with non-recourse loans, investor-owned life insurance indicators, irrevocable trust ownership patterns, life settlement broker involvement, rapid policy transfer intent, unusual beneficiary designations), investigation status, compliance review outcome, state-specific STOLI statute compliance check, SIU referral flag, and STOLI determination (cleared, confirmed, inconclusive). Also captures NAR (Net Amount at Risk) calculations, NAR calculation method, and whether NAR triggers reinsurance cession thresholds. Represents the underwriter's formal holistic risk evaluation tied to a specific application. Sourced from the Underwriting Workbench automated rules engine and manual underwriter review.
products.reference: NAIC Underwriting Guidelines; MIB Risk Classification

products.name: evidence_requirement
products.description: Consolidated master record for all underwriting evidence items ordered, received, and reviewed for a specific application or policy change re-underwriting case. Encompasses all evidence types and their type-specific detail attributes: Attending Physician Statements (APS) with physician name, practice, NPI, request/received dates, medical conditions disclosed, treatment history, medications, lab results, and underwriter review notes; paramedical examinations with exam vendor (ExamOne, APPS), examiner details, exam date/location, height, weight, blood pressure, pulse, specimen collection status, lab results summary, and completion status; MIB inquiries with submission date, MIB member code, applicant consent flag, response codes, condition codes returned, follow-up action required flag, and review status; EKG, blood profiles, urine specimens, treadmill stress tests, financial statements, inspection reports, MVR, prescription drug history (Rx check), cognitive assessments, and functional capacity evaluations. Tracks ordering date, vendor assigned, received date, evidence status (ordered, in-transit, received, under-review, satisfied, waived), evidence type classification, and type-specific extended attributes. Manages the complete evidence workflow within the Underwriting Workbench. Supports both traditional and accelerated underwriting evidence protocols. Subject to HIPAA data handling requirements for medical evidence, FCRA compliance for consumer report evidence, and MIB Group data use agreements.

attributes.name: inquiry_type

attributes.name: response_received_timestamp

attributes.name: stoli_indicator_flag

attributes.name: underwriter_notes

attributes.name: underwriter_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the underwriters review of the MIB inquiry results. Tracks the progression of manual underwriting analysis.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this MIB inquiry record was last updated. Tracks modifications to inquiry status, review status, or underwriter notes.

products.name: rule
products.description: Master reference catalog of all underwriting rules, medical impairment rating guidelines, and underwriting manual entries configured in the automated rules engine. For automated rules: stores rule code, rule name, rule category (medical, financial, product eligibility, STOLI detection), rule logic description, effective date, expiration date, product line applicability, face amount threshold, age band applicability, and rule owner. For medical impairment guidelines: stores impairment code, impairment name (e.g., Type 2 Diabetes, Coronary Artery Disease, Sleep Apnea), ICD-10 code mapping, standard rating action (table rating range, flat extra range, decline threshold), age and severity modifiers, and source (company manual or reinsurer guide). Provides the authoritative catalog of all automated underwriting rules and medical impairment rating guidelines governing NB decisioning and risk classification. Replaces the need for a separate impairment guide entity.

attributes.name: flat_extra_per_thousand_max
attributes.description: Maximum flat extra premium charge per thousand dollars of face amount. Defines the upper bound of the flat extra surcharge. Null if rule does not use flat extras.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Guidelines, Reinsurer Rating Manuals

attributes.name: flat_extra_per_thousand_min
attributes.description: Minimum flat extra premium charge per thousand dollars of face amount, expressed in dollars. Used for temporary or permanent extra mortality charges. Null if rule does not use flat extras.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Guidelines, Reinsurer Rating Manuals

attributes.name: gender_applicability
attributes.description: Specifies whether the rule applies to male applicants, female applicants, or all genders. Supports gender-specific medical underwriting criteria (e.g., prostate conditions for males, pregnancy-related conditions for females).

attributes.name: icd10_code_mapping
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Code Mapping
attributes.description: ICD-10 diagnosis code(s) associated with the medical impairment. Supports integration with Attending Physician Statements (APS) and medical records. Multiple codes may be comma-separated. Null for non-medical rules.

attributes.name: impairment_code
attributes.description: Standard code identifying a specific medical impairment or health condition (e.g., DIAB2 for Type 2 Diabetes, CAD for Coronary Artery Disease). Used for medical underwriting and impairment rating. Null for non-medical rules.
attributes.references: MIB Group Impairment Codes, Reinsurer Medical Manuals

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this rule record. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: logic_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the rule logic, conditions, and decision criteria. Explains how the rule evaluates applicant data and what actions it triggers. Critical for underwriter training and audit compliance.

attributes.name: nar_calculation_impact
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Amount at Risk (NAR) Calculation Impact
attributes.description: Describes how this rule affects the Net Amount at Risk (NAR) calculation. NAR is the death benefit minus the policy cash value or account value. Rules that increase mortality risk typically increase NAR exposure.
attributes.references: NAIC Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP), Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional context, special instructions, or clarifications related to the rule. Used by underwriters and rule administrators for operational guidance.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the business unit, underwriting team, or individual responsible for maintaining and updating this rule. Supports governance and accountability.

attributes.name: product_line_applicability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of product lines to which this rule applies (e.g., Term Life, Whole Life, Universal Life, Indexed Universal Life, Variable Universal Life, Fixed Annuity, Variable Annuity). Null or 'all' if rule applies universally.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rule requires state insurance department approval before implementation. True for rules affecting rate classes, policy forms, or underwriting practices subject to regulatory filing requirements.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, State Insurance Department Filing Requirements

attributes.name: reinsurance_cession_impact
attributes.description: Indicates how this rule affects reinsurance placement decisions: automatic (ceded under automatic treaty), facultative (requires facultative reinsurance submission), retained (risk retained by direct writer), or none (no reinsurance impact).
attributes.references: Reinsurance Treaty Terms, NAIC Reinsurance Standards

attributes.name: rule_category
attributes.description: Classification of the rule type. Medical rules evaluate health conditions and impairments; financial rules assess income and net worth; product eligibility rules determine product suitability; STOLI detection rules identify stranger-originated life insurance; AML/KYC rules support anti-money laundering compliance; age band rules apply age-specific underwriting criteria.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the rule within the automated rules engine or underwriting manual. Used for system integration and rule invocation.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the underwriting rule or medical impairment guideline. Provides clear identification for underwriters and business users.

attributes.name: rule_source
attributes.description: Origin of the rule: company underwriting manual (proprietary guidelines), reinsurer guide (reinsurer-provided rating manual), regulatory requirement (mandated by state or federal regulation), or industry standard (NAIC, ACORD, MIB best practices).

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rule. Active rules are in production use; inactive rules are disabled; pending approval rules await governance review; retired rules are archived; suspended rules are temporarily disabled pending review.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rule is executed automatically by the rules engine, serves as a manual guideline for underwriter reference, defines an impairment rating action, triggers an automatic decline, or triggers a referral to senior underwriter or medical director.

attributes.name: smoker_status_applicability
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rule applies to smokers, non-smokers, or all applicants. Supports tobacco-use-specific underwriting criteria and rating adjustments.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system from which this rule was sourced (e.g., RGAX AURA, Swiss Re Magnum, proprietary underwriting workbench). Supports data lineage and integration troubleshooting.

attributes.name: standard_rating_action
attributes.description: Default underwriting action prescribed by the rule: standard (no extra premium), table rating (mortality multiplier), flat extra (per-thousand charge), decline (application rejected), or refer (escalate to senior underwriter or medical director).
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Guidelines, Reinsurer Rating Manuals

attributes.name: table_rating_range_max
attributes.description: Maximum table rating (A through P) for the impairment or risk factor. Defines the upper bound of mortality surcharge. Null if rule does not use table ratings.
attributes.references: NAIC Table Rating Standards, Reinsurer Rating Manuals

attributes.name: table_rating_range_min
attributes.description: Minimum table rating (A through P) for the impairment or risk factor. Table ratings represent mortality multipliers (e.g., Table B = 150% of standard mortality). Null if rule does not use table ratings.
attributes.references: NAIC Table Rating Standards, Reinsurer Rating Manuals

attributes.name: underwriting_method_applicability
attributes.description: Specifies the underwriting method(s) to which this rule applies: full underwriting (medical exams, APS), simplified issue (health questions only), guaranteed issue (no health questions), accelerated underwriting (automated data sources), or all methods.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the rule. Incremented with each update to support change tracking and historical analysis. Version 1 is the initial rule definition.

products.name: reinsurance_placement
products.description: Consolidated underwriting reinsurance placement, cession decision, and retention limit record for a specific application. Encompasses the full reinsurance placement workflow: retention limit schedule (product line, plan code, insured age band, gender, risk class, retention limit amount, effective date, reinsurance treaty reference), NAR-based cession threshold evaluation, placement type determination (automatic YRT/coinsurance vs. facultative). For automatic placements: treaty reference, cession amount, and automatic binding confirmation. For facultative placements: submission date, reinsurer(s) submitted to, case summary, medical and financial evidence package transmitted, reinsurer offer details (risk class, table rating, flat extra, exclusions, offer expiration date), accepted offer reference, and facultative placement workflow status from submission through acceptance. Stores reinsurer selected, reinsurer decision, reinsurer risk class assigned, and overall placement status. Bridges the underwriting domain to the reinsurance domain for NAR-based cession decisions made at the time of underwriting.
products.reference: YRT; Coinsurance; Facultative Reinsurance; ACORD Reinsurance Standards

products.name: rule_execution_result
products.description: This association product represents the Event between rules_engine_output and rule. It captures the outcome of evaluating one specific underwriting rule within one specific rules engine execution. Each record links one rules_engine_output to one rule and carries the per-rule result data (outcome, score, sequence, override) that exists only in the context of that rule being fired within that evaluation. Provides the granular audit trail required for STP rate analysis, rule performance monitoring, and regulatory examination of automated underwriting decisions.. Existence Justification: In automated underwriting, a rules engine evaluation (rules_engine_output) fires multiple individual rules against a single application, and each rule (rule) is fired across thousands of evaluations over its lifetime. The relationship between a specific evaluation and a specific rule is a discrete operational event — a 'fired rule' — that carries its own result data (pass/fail/refer, score, sequence, override). This is not derivable from either entity alone; the per-rule outcome within a specific evaluation is the core audit record of automated underwriting decisioning.

attributes.name: rule_execution_result_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Rule Execution Result - Rule Execution Result Id
attributes.description: Primary key for the rule_execution_result association

attributes.name: rule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific underwriting rule that was evaluated

attributes.name: rules_engine_output_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Rule Execution Result - Rules Engine Output Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the rules engine evaluation in which this rule was fired

attributes.name: decline_reason_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of reason codes for rules that triggered an automated decline recommendation. Used for adverse action notices and regulatory compliance. [Moved from rules_engine_output: This comma-separated string on rules_engine_output is a denormalized encoding of individual rule FAIL outcomes. Each decline reason code corresponds to a specific rule that fired with a FAIL result. The correct model is one rule_execution_result record per fired rule with result=FAIL, making this field redundant and replaceable by querying the association table.]

attributes.name: execution_sequence
attributes.description: The ordinal position in which this rule was evaluated within the rules engine execution. Critical for audit and debugging purposes, as rule execution order can affect downstream rule conditions in chained rule logic.

attributes.name: fired_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rule actually triggered (fired) during the evaluation. A rule may be in scope for an evaluation but not fire if its preconditions were not met. Distinguishes between rules that were evaluated and rules that actively influenced the decision.

attributes.name: override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a human underwriter overrode the automated result of this specific rule. Supports underwriter override tracking, exception reporting, and model performance monitoring.

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: Free-text justification provided by the underwriter when overriding this rule's automated result. Populated only when override_flag is TRUE. Supports audit trail, compliance review, and underwriter decision quality monitoring.

attributes.name: refer_reason_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of reason codes for rules that triggered a refer outcome, requiring human underwriter review. Each code represents a specific underwriting concern or exception. [Moved from rules_engine_output: This comma-separated string on rules_engine_output is a denormalized encoding of individual rule REFER outcomes. Each refer reason code corresponds to a specific rule that fired with a REFER result. The correct model is one rule_execution_result record per fired rule with result=REFER, making this field redundant and replaceable by querying the association table.]

attributes.name: result
attributes.description: The outcome of evaluating this specific rule within this evaluation. PASS indicates the applicant met the rule criteria, FAIL indicates a decline trigger, REFER indicates the rule routed the case to a human underwriter, NOT_APPLICABLE indicates the rule was loaded but conditions for firing were not met.

attributes.name: score
attributes.description: Numeric score or weight contributed by this rule to the overall evaluation. Used in scoring-based rules engines where individual rule contributions are summed or weighted to produce the final automated decision recommendation.

domains.name: claims
domains.description: Manages the full claims adjudication and settlement lifecycle for death benefits (DB), disability income (DI), LTC, living benefits, and waiver-of-premium claims. Owns claim intake, FNOL, investigation, fraud detection, beneficiary verification, contestability review, settlement calculations (DB, GMDB, GMIB), payment disbursement, and claim closure. Tracks IBNR reserves and integrates with reinsurance recoverables for ceded claim recovery.

products.name: claim
products.description: Core master record for every life insurance and annuity claim filed against a policy or contract. Captures the full claim lifecycle from FNOL (First Notice of Loss) through adjudication, settlement, and closure. Tracks claim type (DB, DI, LTC, GMDB, GMIB, living benefit, waiver-of-premium), claim status, cause of loss (death, disability, chronic/critical illness, terminal illness), contestability period flag, policy reference, claimant identity, date of loss, date reported, assigned examiner, examiner assignment history, and claim disposition. Supports all claim types for life, annuity, and rider benefits. SSOT for all claim identity, lifecycle state, and examiner assignment within the claims domain.

products.name: claim_investigation
products.description: Tracks all formal investigation workflows for claims requiring scrutiny beyond standard adjudication, including Special Investigations Unit (SIU) referrals, contestability reviews, and field investigations. CONTESTABILITY: covers claims within the 2-year contestability window — application misrepresentation findings, medical history discrepancies, MIB report findings, and rescission recommendations. FRAUD/SIU: covers fraud referral triggers, SIU case numbers, fraud indicator scoring, law enforcement referrals, state DOI fraud bureau filings (per NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act), and NICB database checks. GENERAL INVESTIGATION: covers cause-of-death investigations, APS requests, MIB record reviews, STOLI/stranger-originated life insurance investigations, and field investigations. Records investigation type, escalation level (standard, SIU referral, law enforcement), assigned investigator, investigation open/close dates, findings summary, investigation disposition (substantiated, unsubstantiated, closed without action, rescind policy, pay in full, reduce benefit), and regulatory reporting obligations. SSOT for all claim investigation, fraud referral, and contestability review activity within the claims domain.

products.name: adjudication
products.description: Core transactional record capturing the formal adjudication decision for a claim, including full denial documentation and adverse action lifecycle when applicable. Records adjudication outcome (approved, denied, partially approved, pended, rescinded), adjudication date, examiner ID, decision basis (policy provisions applied: suicide exclusion, contestability, misrepresentation, exclusion riders), benefit amount approved, supervisor review flag, and authority level applied. For approved claims: captures the selected settlement method and election details (elected option, payment frequency, tax withholding preference, beneficiary signature confirmation) as the SSOT for the adjudication-time settlement decision. For denial outcomes: captures denial reason codes (per NAIC and state DOI standards), policy provision cited, denial letter generation date, adverse action notice compliance flag, claimant appeal rights disclosure, external review referral flag, internal review completion date, and litigation hold management. Supports state prompt payment law compliance and DOI complaint tracking. SSOT for all claim adjudication decisions and adverse actions within the claims domain. Note: settlement election details here record the decision-time election; claim_payment records the execution-time disbursement details.

products.name: living_benefit_claim
products.description: Consolidated claim detail record for all living-insured benefit claims including Disability Income (DI), Long-Term Care (LTC), Accelerated Death Benefit (ADB), chronic/critical illness riders, GMIB/GMWB annuity guarantees, and Waiver-of-Premium (WP) claims. Captures claim subtype, triggering event (disability onset, terminal/chronic/critical illness diagnosis, ADL impairment, cognitive impairment), elimination period tracking, benefit calculation basis, payment frequency and duration, ongoing eligibility verification requirements, medical documentation (ICD-10 codes, APS, functional capacity evaluations), disability definition applied (own-occ, any-occ, modified own-occ), care setting (for LTC: home health, assisted living, nursing facility), Social Security offset (for DI), coordination of benefits with Medicare/Medicaid (for LTC), tax treatment (IRC 101(g) for ADB), waiver trigger and premium amount waived (for WP), inflation protection adjustment (for LTC), and termination/recovery events. Extends the core claim record with type-specific attributes while sharing the common claim lifecycle. SSOT for all non-death-benefit claim detail within the claims domain — replaces standalone DI, LTC, and waiver-of-premium claim records.

ADLs typically include bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transferring, and continence. Most LTC policies require impairment in 2 or more ADLs for benefit eligibility. SSOT for all claim disbursement transactions and payment execution within the claims domain. Note: the adjudication record captures the decision-time settlement election; this product records the actual payment execution.

products.name: claim_reserve
products.description: Actuarial reserve record tracking claim-level case reserves and portfolio-level IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) estimates for claims liability management. CASE RESERVES: captures initial and current reserve amounts per open claim, reserve change history with reason codes, reserve adequacy review dates, reserving examiner, and reserve release upon claim closure. IBNR ESTIMATES: captures estimation period (month-end, quarter-end, year-end), estimation methodology (chain-ladder development, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, frequency-severity), estimated IBNR amount by claim type (DB, DI, LTC, living benefit), confidence intervals, loss development factors, prior period IBNR comparison, estimating actuary ID, and actuarial sign-off/approval status. BULK RESERVES: captures supplemental reserves for catastrophic events or emerging trends. Tracks SAP and GAAP reserve basis and supports LDTI (ASC 944), PBR (VM-20/VM-21), and ORSA reserve adequacy assessments. Feeds actuarial and finance domains for statutory reporting (Annual Statement Schedule P equivalent for life). SSOT for all claim-level case reserves, portfolio-level IBNR estimates, and bulk reserve balances within the claims domain.

domains.name: billing
domains.description: SSOT for all premium billing, collection, and payment processing activities. Owns premium schedules, modal billing (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly), grace period management, lapse administration, reinstatement processing, NSF handling, EFT/ACH payment records, APE calculations, premium allocation across policy components (base, riders, COI), and automatic premium loan (APL) triggers.

products.name: premium_schedule
products.description: Master record defining the premium payment schedule for a policy, including modal frequency (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly), scheduled premium amounts, APE calculations, billing method (direct bill, EFT/ACH, payroll deduction, list bill), and billing day-of-month. Serves as the authoritative source for what is owed and when for each policy. Owned by the Billing and Premium Collection System (Sapiens BillingPro / Majesco Billing).

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded description of the reason for the most recent amendment to this premium schedule (e.g., 'modal frequency change', 'face amount increase', 'rider addition', 'reinstatement'). Populated when schedule_version > 1. Supports audit trail and policyholder service history.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: ape_amount
attributes.description: Annual Premium Equivalent (APE) representing the annualized value of the modal premium. Calculated as the modal premium multiplied by the modal frequency factor (e.g., monthly × 12). Used for new business reporting, sales performance measurement, and actuarial valuation inputs per industry APE conventions.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Annual Statement; IFRS 17

attributes.name: apl_activated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) feature is currently active on this schedule. When True, the billing system has been configured to execute APL draws upon premium non-payment. Distinct from apl_eligible which reflects product eligibility.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: apl_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the policy is eligible for Automatic Premium Loan (APL) processing. When True, the billing system will automatically trigger a policy loan to cover an unpaid premium before the policy lapses, provided sufficient cash surrender value (CSV) exists. Applicable to whole life and universal life products.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; IRC Section 7702; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: base_premium_amount
attributes.description: The annualized premium attributable to the base policy coverage only, excluding rider premiums. Used for premium allocation across policy components (base vs. riders) and for Cost of Insurance (COI) calculations in universal life products.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; IRC Section 7702; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: billing_day_of_month
attributes.description: The day of the month on which the premium billing notice is generated and/or the EFT/ACH debit is initiated. Valid values are 1 through 28 (capped at 28 to avoid month-end variability). Stored in the billing system as the recurring debit/invoice trigger date.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NACHA ACH Operating Rules

attributes.name: billing_method
attributes.description: The method by which premiums are collected from the policyholder. 'direct_bill' sends invoices directly to the insured; 'eft_ach' uses Electronic Funds Transfer / Automated Clearing House (EFT/ACH) for automatic bank debits; 'payroll_deduction' applies to employer-sponsored plans; 'list_bill' is used for group or association billing; 'bank_draft' is a pre-authorized bank withdrawal. Drives payment processing workflow in Sapiens BillingPro / Majesco Billing.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NACHA ACH Operating Rules; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: billing_notice_preference
attributes.description: The policyholder's preferred channel for receiving premium billing notices and payment reminders. 'paper' sends physical mail; 'email' sends electronic notices; 'sms' sends text message reminders; 'portal' delivers notices via the insurer's online self-service portal; 'none' suppresses notices (e.g., for EFT/ACH auto-pay enrollees).
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; State Department of Insurance e-delivery regulations

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this premium schedule record was first created in the billing system. Represents the business event time of schedule establishment, which typically coincides with policy issuance or a subsequent schedule amendment. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this premium schedule (e.g., USD). Required for multi-currency policy administration and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this premium schedule becomes binding and the first premium is due. Aligns with the policy issue date or the date of a schedule amendment (e.g., modal frequency change, face amount change).
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; IRC Section 7702

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this premium schedule ends. Null for open-ended schedules (e.g., whole life). Populated for term policies at the end of the premium-paying period or upon policy maturity.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: grace_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days after the premium due date during which the policy remains in force without payment. Standard grace period is 30 or 31 days per NAIC model regulations. After expiry of the grace period without payment, the policy enters lapse administration processing.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; State Department of Insurance regulations

attributes.name: guideline_annual_premium
attributes.business_glossary_term: Guideline Annual Premium (GAP) — Guideline Premium Test (GPT)
attributes.description: The Guideline Annual Premium (GAP) used in the Guideline Premium Test (GPT) under IRC Section 7702 to determine whether the policy qualifies as life insurance for tax purposes. Calculated by the actuarial system. Premiums paid must not exceed the greater of the GAP or the Guideline Single Premium (GSP).
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702; IRS regulations; Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: lapse_date
attributes.description: The date on which the policy lapsed due to non-payment of premium beyond the grace period. Null for active schedules. Populated by the lapse administration module of the billing system. Critical for lapse experience studies and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; State Department of Insurance regulations; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: last_paid_date
attributes.description: The date through which the policy is paid up based on the most recent premium payment received. Used to determine the paid-to date for policy servicing, lapse calculations, and reinstatement eligibility.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: limited_pay_years
attributes.description: Number of years over which premiums are payable for limited-pay policies (e.g., 10-pay, 20-pay, paid-up at 65). Null when premium_paying_period is not 'limited_pay'. Used to calculate the schedule expiry date and for MEC testing under IRC Section 7702A.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702A; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: mec_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the policy has been classified as a Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) under IRC Section 7702A. 'non_mec' policies retain favorable tax treatment; 'mec' policies are subject to LIFO tax treatment on distributions; 'pending_test' indicates the 7-pay test is in progress. Critical for tax compliance reporting to the IRS.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702A; IRS Publication 575; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: modal_factor
attributes.description: The multiplier applied to the annual premium to derive the modal premium amount for the selected billing frequency. Reflects the cost of installment billing (e.g., monthly factor ≈ 0.0875, quarterly ≈ 0.26, semi-annual ≈ 0.51, annual = 1.0). Stored for audit and recalculation purposes.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation; Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: modal_frequency
attributes.description: The payment frequency selected by the policyholder for premium remittance. Determines the billing cycle and the modal premium amount applied. Standard life insurance modal frequencies per ACORD and NAIC conventions.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: modal_premium_amount
attributes.description: The scheduled premium amount due at each billing interval as determined by the selected modal frequency. Reflects the base policy premium plus any rider premiums and modal loading factor. This is the gross amount billed to the policyholder per billing cycle.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; IRC Section 7702; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: next_due_date
attributes.description: The date on which the next scheduled premium payment is due from the policyholder. Updated by the billing engine after each successful payment or following a reinstatement. Critical for grace period tracking and lapse administration.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: nsf_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) / returned payment events on this premium schedule. Used to assess payment reliability, trigger EFT/ACH suspension, and support fraud detection and AML monitoring per FinCEN BSA requirements.
attributes.references: NACHA ACH Operating Rules; FinCEN BSA/AML requirements; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: nsf_fee_amount
attributes.description: The fee charged to the policyholder per Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) / returned payment event, as defined in the policy contract and state regulations. Used for billing reconciliation and policyholder account management.
attributes.references: NACHA ACH Operating Rules; State Department of Insurance regulations

attributes.name: paid_to_date
attributes.description: The date through which the policy coverage is fully funded by premiums received. Distinct from last_paid_date in that it reflects the coverage period end rather than the transaction date. Used in policy servicing, reinstatement, and lapse administration workflows.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: premium_paying_period
attributes.description: Defines the duration over which premiums are payable under the policy contract. 'whole_life' requires premiums for the life of the insured; 'limited_pay' specifies a fixed number of years; 'single_premium' is a one-time payment; 'term_to_age' requires premiums until a specified attained age. Drives schedule expiry and Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) testing.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702; IRC Section 7702A (MEC); ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: reinstatement_date
attributes.description: The date on which a lapsed policy's premium schedule was reinstated following payment of overdue premiums and satisfaction of reinstatement requirements. Null for schedules that have never lapsed. Used in reinstatement processing and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; State Department of Insurance regulations

attributes.name: rider_premium_amount
attributes.description: The annualized premium attributable to all policy riders combined (e.g., Accidental Death Benefit (ADB), Waiver of Premium, Long-Term Care (LTC) rider). Supports premium allocation reporting and rider-level profitability analysis.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: schedule_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this premium schedule, as assigned by the Billing and Premium Collection System (e.g., Sapiens BillingPro). Used in policyholder correspondence, billing notices, and reconciliation with payment records.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the premium schedule. Drives billing engine behavior: 'active' schedules generate billing notices; 'suspended' schedules are on hold (e.g., waiver of premium); 'lapsed' indicates non-payment past grace period; 'reinstated' follows successful reinstatement processing; 'cancelled' or 'terminated' are end-states. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|suspended|lapsed|reinstated|cancelled|terminated — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Sapiens BillingPro lifecycle states

attributes.name: schedule_version
attributes.description: Monotonically incrementing version number for this premium schedule record. Incremented each time the schedule is amended (e.g., modal frequency change, face amount change, rider addition/removal). Supports audit trail and temporal data management in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: seven_pay_premium_limit
attributes.description: The maximum cumulative premium that can be paid in the first seven policy years without triggering Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) classification under IRC Section 7702A. Calculated by the actuarial system and stored here for billing compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702A; IRS Publication 575; Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this premium schedule record was sourced (e.g., Sapiens BillingPro, Majesco Billing). Used for data lineage tracking, ETL reconciliation, and Silver Layer data quality management in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this premium schedule record in the billing system. Updated on any field change including status transitions, payment date updates, and schedule amendments. Used for incremental ETL processing and audit trail in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: waiver_of_premium
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Waiver of Premium (WP) benefit is currently active on this schedule, typically triggered by the insured's disability. When True, scheduled premiums are waived and the billing engine suspends premium collection while keeping the policy in force.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Disability Income Regulation; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: waiver_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Waiver of Premium (WP) benefit became effective for this schedule. Null when waiver_of_premium is False. Used to track the duration of the waiver period and for actuarial experience studies.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Disability Income Regulation; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

products.name: premium_bill
products.description: Transactional record of each billing cycle demand and all associated notices sent to policyholders or group administrators. Captures bill date, due date, grace period expiry date, billed amount, modal premium, outstanding balance, notice type (initial bill, reminder, grace warning, final notice, lapse notice, reinstatement offer, NSF notification, APL notification), delivery method (mail, email, EFT notice, SMS), delivery date, delivery confirmation, bill status (issued, paid, partial, lapsed, cancelled), and regulatory notice requirement reference including state DOI mandated notice timelines. Serves as SSOT for all premium billing demands and billing-related communications. Analogous to an invoice plus its delivery confirmation and notice audit trail in the insurance billing context. Source system: Sapiens BillingPro / Majesco Billing.

attributes.name: premium_bill_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each premium billing demand record in the Sapiens BillingPro / Majesco Billing system. Serves as the primary key for the premium_bill data product.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; Sapiens BillingPro Data Model

attributes.name: account_id

attributes.name: billing_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: Premium bills generate regulatory billing notices, lapse warnings, and payment statements that must be retained for compliance and customer service. Real business process: state insurance law complian

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to annuity.annuity_contract. Business justification: Premium bills are issued for premium-paying annuity contracts. Currently premium_bill only has in_force_policy_id for life policies. A direct annuity_contract_id FK supports annuity billing statement

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the life insurance policy for which this billing demand is generated. Links the bill to the master policy record in the Policy Administration System.
attributes.references: ACORD Life Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: insured_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policyholder.insured. Business justification: State DOI regulations require premium bills to identify the insured. Waiver-of-premium billing notices and disability waiver activation are insured-specific. Customer service bill lookup by insured is

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
