attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this retention limit record was formally approved by the authorized actuarial or reinsurance management authority. Required for SOX compliance and internal governance documentation of limit changes.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation; ORSA Guidance Manual

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual (typically Chief Actuary, VP Reinsurance, or CRO) who authorized this retention limit record. Supports governance, audit trail, and SOX internal control requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation; ERM Framework

attributes.name: cession_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this limit record governs automatic cessions (risks ceded within treaty terms without individual submission), facultative cessions (risks requiring individual reinsurer approval), or facultative-obligatory arrangements. Automatic binding limits apply only to automatic cession type.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this retention limit record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; FASB ASC 944; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: credit_for_reinsurance_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reinsurer qualifies for credit for reinsurance under applicable state insurance law, allowing the ceding company to take a reserve credit on its statutory balance sheet. Determined by reinsurer licensure status and collateral arrangements.
attributes.references: NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law; State Departments of Insurance; SAP Accounting Principles

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the limit amount is denominated (e.g., USD). Required for multi-currency treaty arrangements and international reinsurance partners.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this retention or binding limit record becomes operative and governs cession routing decisions. Aligns with treaty effective dates and policy year boundaries.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this retention or binding limit record ceases to be operative. Null indicates an open-ended limit with no scheduled expiration. Used in conjunction with effective_date to determine the applicable limit for a given valuation or cession date.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: flat_extra_max
attributes.description: The maximum flat extra premium per thousand of face amount (expressed in dollars per thousand) eligible for automatic cession under this limit. Risks with flat extras exceeding this threshold require facultative submission. Null indicates no flat extra restriction.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Underwriting Standards

attributes.name: gender
attributes.description: Gender classification band to which this retention limit applies. Some treaty structures differentiate retention limits by gender due to mortality table differences. Unisex indicates the limit applies to all genders. Null indicates no gender restriction.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: jumbo_limit_amount
attributes.description: The absolute maximum face amount threshold above which facultative reinsurance submission is required, regardless of whether the risk falls within the automatic binding limit. Risks exceeding the jumbo limit cannot be automatically ceded and must be individually underwritten by the reinsurer. Null if this record is not of type jumbo_limit.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: limit_amount
attributes.description: The principal monetary threshold value for this limit record, expressed in the applicable currency. For retention_per_life and retention_per_policy, this is the maximum net face amount retained by the company. For automatic_binding_limit, this is the maximum face amount that can be auto-ceded. For jumbo_limit, this is the threshold above which facultative submission is mandatory. Drives the cession routing decision engine.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance — Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: limit_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this retention or binding limit configuration within the reinsurance management system (e.g., RET-WL-NS-M-01). Used as the business key for cross-system reference and bordereaux reporting.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance — Treaty Management Module; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: limit_description
attributes.description: Free-text description providing additional context about this retention limit record, including any special conditions, exceptions, or treaty-specific notes that are not captured in structured fields. Used by reinsurance analysts and actuaries for reference.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: limit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the retention limit record. Active records drive live cession routing decisions. Superseded records have been replaced by a newer version. Expired records are past their effective period. Pending records are approved but not yet in effect.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the limit record: retention_per_life (maximum net amount retained across all policies on a single life), retention_per_policy (maximum net amount retained on a single policy), automatic_binding_limit (maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission), or jumbo_limit (threshold above which facultative reinsurance submission is required regardless of treaty).
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: nar_basis
attributes.description: Specifies the basis on which the retention limit amount is measured: face_amount (total death benefit face), NAR (Net Amount at Risk — death benefit minus reserve), account_value (for UL/IUL/FIA products), or death_benefit (total contractual death benefit including riders). Drives the NAR-based cession calculation methodology.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: per_life_limit_amount
attributes.description: The maximum total net amount the company will retain across all policies insuring the same life (insured). When total in-force exposure on a single life exceeds this threshold, the excess must be ceded. Critical for managing concentration risk on high-value lives.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: policy_year_max
attributes.description: The maximum policy year (inclusive) for which this retention limit applies. Null indicates the limit applies through the end of the policy term. Used in conjunction with policy_year_min to define the policy year band.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: policy_year_min
attributes.description: The minimum policy year (inclusive) for which this retention limit applies. Some treaties define different retention schedules for early policy years versus later years, particularly for YRT (Yearly Renewable Term) treaties where NAR changes over time.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: rate_table_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the actuarial rate table used to derive the retention limit amounts (e.g., 2017CSO, 2001CSO, company-specific mortality table). Ensures traceability between limit values and the underlying actuarial assumptions used in their derivation.
attributes.references: Actuarial Valuation System — AXIS; Prophet; NAIC Model Regulation; PBR Compliance

attributes.name: rbc_credit_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether cessions made under this retention limit qualify for RBC (Risk-Based Capital) credit under NAIC RBC formula requirements. RBC-eligible cessions reduce the company's required capital, making this flag critical for capital optimization and ORSA reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC RBC Model Act; NAIC Model Regulation; ORSA Guidance Manual

attributes.name: smoker_status
attributes.description: Tobacco use classification band to which this retention limit applies. Smoker and non-smoker populations carry materially different mortality rates, often resulting in distinct retention schedules. Null indicates the limit applies regardless of smoker status.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Underwriting Standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this retention limit record originated (e.g., SWISS_RE_IRIS, RGA_AURA, INTERNAL_TREATY_MGR). Supports data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: source_system_limit_ref
attributes.description: The native identifier or reference number assigned to this retention limit record in the originating operational system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS internal limit ID). Enables cross-system reconciliation and traceability from the silver layer back to the source system.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: table_rating_max
attributes.description: The maximum substandard table rating (expressed as a letter A–P or numeric percentage, e.g., Table D or 150%) eligible for automatic cession under this limit. Risks with table ratings exceeding this threshold require facultative submission regardless of face amount.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Underwriting Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this retention limit record was last modified. Tracks changes to limit amounts, effective dates, or status. Supports audit trail and change management requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; FASB ASC 944; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this retention limit record. Incremented each time the limit is revised. Enables tracking of limit changes over time and supports point-in-time queries for historical cession routing validation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation

domains.name: actuarial
domains.description: Owns all actuarial valuation, reserving, and experience study data. Manages GAAP/SAP/IFRS reserve calculations, PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20, cash flow projections, mortality and lapse assumption tables, DAC amortization schedules, LDTI transition adjustments, ALM analysis, and ORSA inputs. Supports Prophet/AXIS/MoSes model outputs, EOY/BOY reserve snapshots, pricing, product development, and ERM frameworks.

products.name: reserve_calculation
products.description: Core actuarial reserve calculation records capturing GAAP, SAP, and IFRS 17 reserve amounts computed per policy cohort or model segment. Stores net premium reserve (NPR), gross premium reserve (GPR), IBNR, PBR deterministic reserve (DR), stochastic reserve (SR), and LDTI liability for future policy benefits (LFPB). Includes point-in-time snapshot data: BOY and EOY reserve balances, net amount at risk (NAR), reserve per unit, and reserve change components (new business, terminations, interest accretion, assumption unlocking). Each record is linked to a parent valuation_run, assumption_set, cohort_definition, and pbr_model_segment. Sourced from Prophet/AXIS/MoSes valuation runs. Represents the primary output of the actuarial valuation cycle for statutory annual statement, GAAP financial close, and IFRS 17 reporting.
products.reference: NAIC VM-20 PBR Reserve; ASC 944 GAAP Reserve; SAP Reserve

attributes.name: reserve_calculation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the reserve calculation record. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: annuitant_id

attributes.name: assumption_set_id
attributes.description: Reference to the actuarial assumption set (mortality, lapse, expense, interest) applied in this reserve calculation.

attributes.name: cohort_definition_id
attributes.description: Reference to the policy cohort definition used for grouped reserve calculations. Cohorts typically group policies by issue year, product type, and underwriting class.

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to annuity.annuity_contract. Business justification: Statutory and GAAP reserves are calculated at the individual annuity contract level. Essential for financial reporting, regulatory filings (Annual Statement), PBR compliance, and reconciliation of agg

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the individual policy or contract for which reserves are calculated. May be null for cohort-level or model-segment-level calculations.

attributes.name: insured_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policyholder.insured. Business justification: Reserve calculations require individual insured characteristics (issue age, attained age, gender, tobacco status, risk class) for accurate mortality and lapse assumptions. Actuaries calculate reserves

attributes.name: mortality_table_id

attributes.name: pbr_model_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the PBR model segment used for VM-20 deterministic and stochastic reserve calculations. Segments group policies by similar risk characteristics.

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Reserve calculations require direct product plan reference for applying product-specific reserve basis rules (statutory/GAAP/IFRS17), PBR model segment assignment, and assumption set selection. Critic

attributes.name: plan_version_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.plan_version. Business justification: Reserves are calculated against a specific plan version — PBR applicability, benefit structures, and reserve basis change with plan version. Statutory reserve reporting and actuarial opinion require v

attributes.name: portfolio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.portfolio. Business justification: PBR (VM-20) and asset adequacy testing require identifying the investment portfolio backing each reserve calculation to apply correct earned rate assumptions and RBC C-3 interest rate risk charges. Ac

attributes.name: premium_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.premium_schedule. Business justification: Net premium reserve calculations under SAP/GAAP require the gross premium, limited pay years, and premium paying period from the billing premium_schedule. Actuarial reserve systems must reference the

attributes.name: scenario_set_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.scenario_set. Business justification: reserve_calculation captures stochastic_reserve_amount and stochastic_scenario_count, indicating it is computed against a set of stochastic scenarios. Adding scenario_set_id normalizes the reference t

attributes.name: valuation_run_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent actuarial valuation run that produced this reserve calculation. Links to the valuation cycle execution (e.g., Q4 2023 year-end valuation).

attributes.name: actuary_name
attributes.description: The name of the qualified actuary responsible for this reserve calculation. Required for statutory opinion and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation

attributes.name: assumption_unlock_amount
attributes.description: The change in reserves due to updates or unlocking of actuarial assumptions (mortality, lapse, expense, interest). Required under LDTI for GAAP reporting.

attributes.name: boy_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The reserve balance at the beginning of the valuation period (typically January 1 for annual valuations). Used for reserve rollforward analysis.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: The actuarial method or formula used for this reserve calculation (e.g., Commissioners Reserve Valuation Method, Gross Premium Valuation, Seriatim Projection, Model Office). Free-text field for method documentation.

attributes.name: calculation_status
attributes.description: The current status of this reserve calculation in the valuation workflow. Tracks progression from draft through final approval.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this reserve calculation record was first created in the system. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: cte_level
attributes.description: The CTE confidence level used for stochastic reserve calculations under VM-20 (e.g., 70 for CTE70, 98 for CTE98). Represents the average of the worst X% of scenarios.

attributes.name: deterministic_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The deterministic reserve calculated under VM-20 using prescribed scenarios. One of the three components (DR, SR, NPR) used to determine the final PBR reserve.

attributes.name: discount_rate
attributes.description: The interest rate used to discount future cash flows in the reserve calculation. May be a statutory rate, GAAP upper-medium grade rate, or IFRS discount curve rate depending on reporting basis.
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, FASB ASC 944, IFRS 17

attributes.name: eoy_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The reserve balance at the end of the valuation period (typically December 31 for annual valuations). Represents the closing liability position.

attributes.name: expense_assumption_amount
attributes.description: The per-policy or per-unit expense assumption used in the reserve calculation. Includes maintenance expenses and overhead allocation.

attributes.name: experience_variance_amount
attributes.description: The change in reserves due to actual experience differing from expected (e.g., actual mortality vs. expected mortality). Component of reserve variance analysis.

attributes.name: interest_accretion_amount
attributes.description: The increase in reserves due to interest accretion at the valuation interest rate during the period. Component of the reserve rollforward.

attributes.name: lapse_assumption_rate
attributes.description: The annual lapse rate assumption applied in the reserve calculation. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 for 5% lapse rate).

attributes.name: model_change_amount
attributes.description: The change in reserves due to changes in the actuarial valuation model, methodology, or system (e.g., migration from AXIS to Prophet). Tracked separately for audit and reconciliation.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: The version identifier of the actuarial model used for this calculation. Critical for model governance, reproducibility, and audit.

attributes.name: net_amount_at_risk
attributes.description: The net amount at risk, calculated as death benefit minus account value or reserve. Represents the insurer's exposure to mortality risk.

attributes.name: net_premium_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The net premium reserve calculated using traditional actuarial methods. One of the three components (DR, SR, NPR) used to determine the final PBR reserve, and serves as the floor.

attributes.name: new_business_reserve_change
attributes.description: The change in reserves attributable to new business issued during the valuation period. Component of the reserve rollforward.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for actuarial notes, assumptions, methodology details, or special considerations for this reserve calculation. Used for documentation and audit trail.

attributes.name: pbr_floor_applied_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the NPR floor was applied in the final PBR reserve calculation. True if the NPR exceeded the greater of DR and SR.

attributes.name: reinsurance_ceded_reserve
attributes.description: The portion of the reserve that has been ceded to reinsurers under reinsurance treaties. Reduces the net reserve liability for the direct writer.

attributes.name: reinsurance_recoverable_amount
attributes.description: The amount recoverable from reinsurers for this reserve. Represents an asset on the balance sheet offsetting the gross reserve liability.

attributes.name: reporting_basis
attributes.description: The accounting or regulatory basis under which this reserve is calculated: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS 17 (International Financial Reporting Standards), PBR (Principle-Based Reserving per VM-20), or Tax basis.

attributes.name: reserve_amount
attributes.description: The calculated reserve amount in the reporting currency. This is the primary liability value for the policy, cohort, or model segment as of the valuation date.

attributes.name: reserve_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the reserve amount (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP).

attributes.name: reserve_per_unit
attributes.description: The reserve amount per unit of coverage (e.g., per $1,000 of face amount). Used for cohort-level and model-segment-level calculations.

attributes.name: reserve_type
attributes.description: The specific type of reserve calculated: NPR (Net Premium Reserve), GPR (Gross Premium Reserve), IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported), DR (Deterministic Reserve per VM-20), SR (Stochastic Reserve per VM-20), LFPB (Liability for Future Policy Benefits under LDTI), CSV (Cash Surrender Value), DAC (Deferred Acquisition Cost), PVFB (Present Value of Future Benefits). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NPR|GPR|IBNR|DR|SR|LFPB|CSV|DAC|PVFB — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The date this reserve calculation was reviewed and approved by the qualified actuary or peer reviewer.

attributes.name: stochastic_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The stochastic reserve calculated under VM-20 using CTE methodology. One of the three components (DR, SR, NPR) used to determine the final PBR reserve.

attributes.name: stochastic_scenario_count
attributes.description: The number of stochastic scenarios run for VM-20 stochastic reserve (SR) calculations. Typically 1,000 to 10,000 scenarios depending on model complexity.

attributes.name: termination_reserve_change
attributes.description: The change in reserves due to policy terminations (deaths, lapses, surrenders, maturities) during the valuation period. Typically a negative value.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this reserve calculation record was last modified. Audit trail field for tracking changes.

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The as-of date for this reserve calculation. Typically end-of-year (EOY) or end-of-quarter (EOQ) for statutory and GAAP reporting.

products.name: valuation_run
products.description: Master record for each actuarial valuation model execution in Prophet, AXIS, or MoSes. Captures run date, valuation basis (BOY/EOY/interim), model version, assumption set used, run type (production/test/pricing), and completion status. Serves as the parent record linking all reserve calculations, cash flow projections, and experience study outputs to a specific model run.

attributes.name: valuation_run_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each actuarial valuation model execution. Primary key for the valuation run record.

attributes.name: actuarial_opinion_document_id

attributes.name: assumption_set_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific set of actuarial assumptions (mortality, lapse, expense, interest rates) applied in this valuation run.

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Valuation runs are scheduled and mandated by specific regulatory obligations (e.g., annual statutory valuation, quarterly LDTI). Compliance tracks which regulatory_obligation triggers each valuation_r

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.scenario_set. Business justification: valuation_run.scenario_count (INT) is an aggregate count of scenarios used in the run, but there is no FK to the scenario_set that defines those scenarios. Adding scenario_set_id → actuarial.scenario_

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the valuation run results were formally approved by the appointed actuary.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation

attributes.name: audit_trail_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this valuation run to detailed audit logs, change control records, and regulatory filing documentation.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Audit Rule, SOX Section 404

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for actuaries to document special considerations, assumption changes, methodology adjustments, or other relevant notes about this valuation run.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this valuation run record was first created in the actuarial data warehouse.

attributes.name: dac_balance
attributes.description: Total Deferred Acquisition Cost asset balance calculated in this valuation run, representing unamortized acquisition expenses under GAAP.

attributes.name: data_extract_date
attributes.description: The date when in-force policy data was extracted from the policy administration system for use in this valuation run.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The policy administration or data warehouse system from which in-force policy data was sourced (e.g., 'FAST', 'Sapiens LifePro', 'Oracle OIPA', 'Enterprise Data Lake').

attributes.name: discount_rate_method
attributes.description: The method used to determine discount rates for present value calculations (e.g., 'Net Portfolio Rate', 'Risk-Free Rate + Spread', 'Prescribed Statutory Rate').
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944-40, NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20

attributes.name: error_log_summary
attributes.description: Summary of errors, warnings, or data quality issues encountered during the valuation run execution, used for troubleshooting and audit trails.

attributes.name: in_force_policy_count
attributes.description: Total number of in-force policies included in the valuation run as of the valuation date.

attributes.name: ldti_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this GAAP valuation run follows the Long Duration Targeted Improvements standard (ASU 2018-12) effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2022.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the actuarial model used for this run, enabling traceability and reproducibility of valuation results.

attributes.name: mortality_table
attributes.description: The mortality table applied in this valuation (e.g., '2017 CSO', '2012 IAM Basic', company-specific experience table).
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, SOA Mortality Tables

attributes.name: output_file_path
attributes.description: File system or cloud storage path where detailed valuation output files (cash flows, seriatim results, summary reports) are stored.

attributes.name: pbr_compliant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this valuation run follows Principle-Based Reserving methodology per NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20 and VM-21 (True) or uses formula-based reserves (False).

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Status of the reconciliation process between valuation results and general ledger or prior period reserves.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404, NAIC Financial Condition Examiners Handbook

attributes.name: reinsurance_included_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether reinsurance ceded and assumed treaties are reflected in the reserve calculations (True) or if this is a gross reserve run (False).

attributes.name: run_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in minutes for the valuation model execution, used for performance monitoring and capacity planning.

attributes.name: run_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the valuation model execution completed (successfully or with errors).

attributes.name: run_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name assigned to the valuation run for identification purposes, often including valuation basis and period (e.g., 'Q4 2023 GAAP Statutory Reserve Calculation').

attributes.name: run_number
attributes.description: Business-facing identifier for the valuation run, typically formatted as YYYY-MM-RUN### for external reference and audit trails.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation

attributes.name: run_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the valuation model execution was initiated.

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current execution and approval status of the valuation run in its lifecycle. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Initiated|Running|Completed|Failed|Cancelled|Under Review|Approved — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: run_type
attributes.description: Classification of the valuation run purpose: Production (official reserves), Test (validation), Pricing (product development), Sensitivity (scenario analysis), Experience Study (assumption review), or Ad Hoc (special analysis).

attributes.name: scenario_count
attributes.description: Number of stochastic economic scenarios executed in this valuation run for PBR or IFRS calculations (typically 1 for deterministic, 1000+ for stochastic).

attributes.name: total_account_value
attributes.description: Aggregate account value across all universal life and annuity contracts included in the valuation, representing policyholder fund balances.

attributes.name: total_face_amount
attributes.description: Aggregate death benefit face amount across all policies included in the valuation, expressed in the reporting currency.

attributes.name: total_reserve_amount
attributes.description: Aggregate reserve liability calculated by this valuation run, representing the present value of future policy benefits and expenses.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this valuation run record was last modified, supporting audit trails and data lineage.

attributes.name: valuation_basis
attributes.description: The accounting or regulatory framework under which reserves are calculated: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP), International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), Tax basis, Principle-Based Reserving (PBR), or Embedded Value.

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The financial reporting date for which reserves and liabilities are being calculated (e.g., December 31, 2023 for year-end valuation).

attributes.name: valuation_period_type
attributes.description: The reporting period classification: Beginning of Year (BOY), End of Year (EOY), Quarterly, Monthly, or Interim valuation snapshot.
attributes.references: NAIC Quarterly and Annual Statement Filing Requirements

attributes.name: variance_from_prior_period
attributes.description: The change in total reserve amount compared to the previous valuation period, used for reserve movement analysis and financial reporting.

attributes.name: voba_balance
attributes.description: Total Value of Business Acquired intangible asset balance for acquired blocks of business, amortized over the life of the policies.

products.name: assumption_set
products.description: Master table defining actuarial assumption sets used in valuation, pricing, and product development models. Captures assumption basis (best estimate, prudent estimate, prescribed, pricing), effective date, product applicability, regulatory basis (GAAP/SAP/IFRS), approval status, and set purpose (valuation, pricing, repricing, experience_update). For pricing-purpose sets, additionally stores profit margin target (ROI/NBV), investment return assumption, expense loading, and regulatory compliance basis (GPT/CVAT for 7702). Each assumption set groups typed assumption_detail records (mortality, lapse, expense, interest rate, morbidity, credibility) into a versioned, auditable package for model governance. Links to product definitions for pricing sets and supports new product development, rate filings, repricing reviews, and experience study assumption updates.
products.reference: Actuarial Assumption Basis; VM-20 Prescribed Assumptions

attributes.name: experience_study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the experience study from which this assumption set was derived or updated. Null if not based on a formal experience study.

attributes.name: parent_assumption_set_id
attributes.description: Reference to the prior version or parent assumption set from which this set was derived. Null if this is the initial version.

attributes.name: approval_date

attributes.description: The assumed annual lapse or surrender rate used in the reserve calculation. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 for 5.00%).
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: ldti_transition_adjustment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Transition Adjustment
attributes.description: The cumulative adjustment to reserves resulting from the adoption of LDTI (Long Duration Targeted Improvements) under FASB ASC 944. Captures the impact of transitioning to updated GAAP reserve methodologies.

attributes.name: nar
attributes.description: The net amount at risk for the insurer, calculated as the death benefit minus the account value or reserve. Key metric for mortality risk exposure.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions, Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: net_reserve
attributes.description: The net reserve after reinsurance cessions. Calculated as reserve_balance minus reinsurance_ceded_reserve.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this reserve snapshot. May include explanations of unusual variances, assumption changes, or special considerations.

attributes.name: pbr_deterministic_reserve
attributes.description: The deterministic reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20. One component of the PBR reserve calculation.

attributes.name: pbr_net_premium_reserve
attributes.description: The net premium reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20. Serves as a floor for the PBR reserve.

attributes.name: pbr_stochastic_reserve
attributes.description: The stochastic reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20 using scenario modeling. One component of the PBR reserve calculation.

attributes.name: product_code
attributes.description: The insurance product code for which reserves are being held. Examples include WL (Whole Life), UL (Universal Life), IUL (Indexed Universal Life), VUL (Variable Universal Life), Term, SPIA (Single Premium Immediate Annuity), FIA (Fixed Indexed Annuity).
attributes.references: Internal Product Catalog, NAIC Product Classification

attributes.name: reinsurance_ceded_reserve
attributes.description: The portion of the reserve that has been ceded to reinsurers under reinsurance treaties. Reduces the net reserve liability for the ceding company.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Schedule S, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: reporting_period
attributes.description: The reporting period this snapshot represents. BOY (Beginning of Year), EOY (End of Year), quarterly (Q1-Q4), or monthly. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BOY|EOY|Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|Monthly — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Quarterly and Annual Statement Filing Requirements

attributes.name: reserve_adequacy_status
attributes.description: The assessment of whether the reserve is adequate to cover expected future obligations. Adequate indicates sufficiency, Deficient indicates shortfall requiring premium deficiency reserve, Redundant indicates excess, Under Review indicates pending actuarial analysis.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944, NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: reserve_balance
attributes.description: The total reserve amount held for this policy or cohort at the snapshot date. Represents the actuarial liability under the specified valuation basis.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Schedule, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: reserve_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reserve being captured. Policy Reserve for contract liabilities, Claim Reserve for known claims, Premium Deficiency Reserve for loss recognition, IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) for estimated unreported claims, Unearned Premium Reserve for prepaid premiums, or Additional Reserve for supplemental reserves.
attributes.value_regex: Policy Reserve|Claim Reserve|Premium Deficiency Reserve|IBNR|Unearned Premium Reserve|Additional Reserve
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: snapshot_date
attributes.description: The valuation date for which this reserve snapshot was calculated. Typically BOY (Beginning of Year) or EOY (End of Year) reporting date.

attributes.name: valuation_basis
attributes.description: The accounting or regulatory basis under which the reserve was calculated. GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards), PBR (Principle-Based Reserving per VM-20), or Tax basis.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944, NAIC SAP, IFRS 17, VM-20

products.name: pricing_basis
products.description: Master table defining actuarial pricing bases for life insurance and annuity products. Captures pricing mortality table, lapse assumption set, expense loading, investment return assumption, profit margin target (ROI/NBV), and regulatory compliance basis (GPT/CVAT for 7702). Links to product definitions and supports new product development, rate filings, and repricing reviews.
products.reference: Actuarial Pricing Basis; IRC 7702 Compliance Basis

attributes.name: pricing_basis_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the actuarial pricing basis record.

attributes.name: assumption_set_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.assumption_set. Business justification: Pricing basis references a specific assumption set used for pricing calculations. The pricing_basis table has mortality_table_code, lapse_assumption_set_code, investment_return_assumption, discount_ra

attributes.name: benefit_structure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.benefit_structure. Business justification: Actuarial pricing sign-off process: pricing basis is constructed per benefit structure (death benefit type, COI structure, nonforfeiture options). Actuaries price each benefit structure variant separa

attributes.name: coi_rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.coi_rate_schedule. Business justification: For UL/VUL products, the pricing basis drives COI rate schedule design. Actuarial pricing sign-off on COI schedules requires tracing each schedule to its pricing basis for IRC 7702 compliance certific

attributes.name: crediting_strategy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.crediting_strategy. Business justification: For IUL/FIA/annuity products, pricing basis sets cap rates, participation rates, and spread rates that define the crediting strategy. Actuarial pricing sign-off on crediting strategies is a named proc

attributes.name: document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: State DOI rate filings and actuarial memoranda require formal pricing basis documentation. Actuaries and compliance teams must link each pricing basis to its supporting regulatory document for rate fi

attributes.name: irc7702_parameter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.irc7702_parameter. Business justification: IRC 7702 parameters (guideline premium, corridor factors, seven-pay limits) directly constrain actuarial pricing for life insurance products. Pricing actuaries must reference irc7702_parameter when se

attributes.name: mortality_table_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.mortality_table. Business justification: Pricing basis directly references a specific mortality table for pricing calculations. The pricing_basis.mortality_table_code attribute should be replaced with a FK to mortality_table.mortality_table_

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the life insurance or annuity product for which this pricing basis applies.

attributes.name: plan_version_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.plan_version. Business justification: Pricing bases are version-specific; rate changes, assumption updates, or filing amendments require new plan versions per state insurance department requirements. Essential for tracking rate action his

attributes.name: policy_form_approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy_form_approval. Business justification: Policy form approvals require actuarial pricing basis for DOI review of rates, benefits, and reserves. Form and rate filings are often submitted together. Links pricing assumptions to approved policy

attributes.name: premium_rate_table_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.premium_rate_table. Business justification: Actuarial pricing process: the pricing basis is the actuarial justification document that produces the premium rate table. Actuaries must trace rate tables back to their pricing basis for state rate f

attributes.name: rate_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.rate_filing. Business justification: Rate filings submitted to DOI require actuarial pricing basis documentation (mortality tables, expense assumptions, profit margins). Pricing basis is the actuarial foundation for rate filing approval.

attributes.name: risk_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to underwriting.risk_class. Business justification: Pricing bases are constructed per underwriting risk class (preferred, standard, substandard) for rate filings and regulatory submissions. Actuaries must trace which canonical risk_class definition dro

attributes.name: underwriting_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.underwriting_class. Business justification: Pricing bases are constructed per underwriting class (smoker_status_pricing_flag, gender_distinct_pricing_flag confirm this segmentation). Actuarial pricing sign-off requires linking each pricing basi

attributes.name: acquisition_expense_rate
attributes.description: Rate or percentage applied to cover first-year acquisition expenses including commissions, underwriting, and policy issuance costs. Expressed as percentage of premium or per-policy amount depending on loading method.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, GAAP ASC 944 DAC

attributes.name: age_basis
attributes.description: Method used to calculate insured age for pricing: ANB (Age Nearest Birthday), ALB (Age Last Birthday), actual (exact age in years and months).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pricing basis was formally approved by the appointed actuary or pricing committee.

attributes.name: approved_by_actuary_name
attributes.description: Name of the qualified actuary (FSA, MAAA) who approved this pricing basis for use.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Opinion Standards, ASOP No. 41

attributes.name: basis_code
attributes.description: Unique business code identifying this pricing basis configuration (e.g., STD_2024_UL, PREF_2023_WL).

attributes.name: basis_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the pricing basis (e.g., Standard Universal Life 2024, Preferred Whole Life 2023).

attributes.name: basis_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pricing basis purpose: new product launch, repricing of existing product, rate revision, competitive market adjustment, regulatory compliance update, or experience study adjustment.

attributes.name: competitive_position_target
attributes.description: Intended competitive positioning of rates under this pricing basis: market_leader (lowest rates), top_quartile, median (middle of market), competitive (within range), value (higher rates, richer benefits).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pricing basis record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: discount_rate
attributes.description: Rate used to discount future cash flows to present value for profit metric calculations (ROI, NBV). May differ from investment return assumption. Expressed as decimal.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this pricing basis becomes applicable for new business or repricing.

attributes.name: expense_loading_method
attributes.description: Method used to load expenses into premium rates: per_policy (flat amount per policy), percent_of_premium (percentage of premium), per_thousand_face_amount (per $1000 of coverage), tiered (varies by band), composite (combination of methods).

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which this pricing basis is no longer valid for new business. Null indicates open-ended applicability.

attributes.name: filing_jurisdiction
attributes.description: State or jurisdiction code (2-letter abbreviation) where this pricing basis was filed for regulatory approval. May be multi-state or nationwide.

attributes.name: gender_distinct_pricing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pricing basis uses gender-distinct mortality and pricing (True) or unisex rates (False). Some jurisdictions prohibit gender-based pricing.
attributes.references: State Insurance Regulations, NAIC Model Laws

attributes.name: investment_return_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed annual investment return rate (net of investment expenses) used in pricing cash flow projections. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.0450 for 4.50%).
attributes.references: NAIC Asset Liability Management Standards, ORSA

attributes.name: maintenance_expense_rate
attributes.description: Rate or percentage applied to cover ongoing policy maintenance and administration expenses in renewal years. Expressed as percentage of premium or per-policy amount depending on loading method.

attributes.name: maximum_face_amount
attributes.description: Maximum death benefit or face amount (in currency) for which this pricing basis applies. Null indicates no upper limit.

attributes.name: maximum_issue_age
attributes.description: Maximum age (in years) at which a policy can be issued under this pricing basis.

attributes.name: minimum_face_amount
attributes.description: Minimum death benefit or face amount (in currency) for which this pricing basis applies.

attributes.name: minimum_issue_age
attributes.description: Minimum age (in years) at which a policy can be issued under this pricing basis.

attributes.name: mortality_improvement_scale
attributes.description: Mortality improvement projection scale applied to base mortality table (e.g., Scale G2, Scale AA, MP-2021). Used to adjust mortality rates for future improvements.
attributes.references: Society of Actuaries Mortality Improvement Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting special considerations, assumptions, limitations, or context for this pricing basis. Used for actuarial documentation and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: pricing_basis_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pricing basis: draft (in development), under_review (actuarial review), approved (ready for use), active (currently in use), superseded (replaced by newer basis), retired (no longer applicable).

attributes.name: pricing_model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the pricing model or software used to generate this basis. Supports model governance and reproducibility.

attributes.name: profit_margin_target_pct
attributes.description: Target profit margin as percentage of premium or present value of profits. Used to calibrate pricing to achieve desired profitability. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.0800 for 8.00%).

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_number
attributes.description: State insurance department filing number or SERFF tracking number associated with the rate filing for this pricing basis. Null if not filed or filed under product filing.

attributes.name: reinsurance_assumption
attributes.description: Type of reinsurance arrangement assumed in pricing: none (no reinsurance), YRT (Yearly Renewable Term), coinsurance, mod_co (modified coinsurance), facultative (case-by-case reinsurance).

attributes.name: reinsurance_cession_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of risk or premium ceded to reinsurers under the assumed reinsurance arrangement. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.9000 for 90% quota share). Null if no reinsurance.

attributes.name: reserve_basis
attributes.description: Accounting or regulatory basis for reserve calculations associated with this pricing: statutory (SAP), GAAP (US GAAP ASC 944), IFRS (IFRS 17), PBR per VM-20 (Principle-Based Reserving), or tax reserves.
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, GAAP ASC 944, IFRS 17

attributes.name: smoker_status_pricing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pricing basis differentiates rates by tobacco/smoker status (True) or uses blended rates (False).

attributes.name: target_nbv
attributes.description: Target new business value per policy or per unit of premium. Represents present value of future profits at issue. Used as profitability benchmark in pricing.
attributes.references: Internal Pricing Standards, IFRS Embedded Value

attributes.name: target_roi
attributes.description: Target return on investment metric used in pricing. Represents expected return on allocated capital. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.1200 for 12.00% ROI).

attributes.name: tax_basis
attributes.description: IRC Section 7702 tax qualification basis for life insurance: GPT (Guideline Premium Test), CVAT (Cash Value Accumulation Test), MEC_compliant (Modified Endowment Contract compliant), non_qualified (not tax-qualified).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pricing basis record was last modified.

products.name: cohort_definition
products.description: Master table defining policy cohorts for LDTI (ASU 2018-12) annual cohort grouping and IFRS 17 group of insurance contracts. Captures cohort grouping criteria (product type, issue year, profitability classification — onerous, profitable, or neither), LDTI transition date, locked-in discount rate, initial LFPB measurement, and IFRS 17 portfolio/group hierarchy. Required for LDTI annual cohort remeasurement, IFRS 17 CSM unit of account, and DAC amortization grouping under ASC 944.
products.reference: LDTI Cohort; IFRS 17 Group of Contracts

attributes.name: cohort_definition_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the cohort definition record. Primary key for the cohort definition entity.

attributes.name: assumption_set_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.assumption_set. Business justification: cohort_definition.mortality_assumption_table (STRING) is a denormalized reference to the mortality assumption used for the cohort. Under LDTI, each cohort has locked-in discount rates and assumptions

attributes.name: benefit_structure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.benefit_structure. Business justification: LDTI cohorts group contracts with similar risk characteristics including benefit structure (death benefit type, nonforfeiture options). ASC 944-40 cohort grouping methodology and IFRS17 group definiti

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: LDTI and IFRS17 cohorts are product-specific groupings by issue year and profitability classification. Each product requires separate cohort tracking for locked-in discount rates, CSM amortization, an

attributes.name: plan_version_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.plan_version. Business justification: LDTI cohorts are established at initial recognition tied to a specific plan version. ASC 944-40 requires cohorts to reflect contracts issued under the same product terms — plan_version captures these

attributes.name: risk_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to underwriting.risk_class. Business justification: LDTI and IFRS17 cohort groupings are defined at initial recognition using underwriting class as a key segmentation dimension. Linking cohort_definition to the canonical risk_class ensures cohort bound

attributes.name: underwriting_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.underwriting_class. Business justification: cohort_definition.underwriting_class is a plain denormalized attribute. LDTI/IFRS17 cohorts are grouped by similar risk characteristics including underwriting class. ASC 944 cohort grouping methodolog

attributes.name: accounting_standard
attributes.description: The accounting framework under which this cohort is defined: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS17 (International Financial Reporting Standards 17), or LDTI (Long Duration Targeted Improvements under ASU 2018-12).

attributes.name: assumption_update_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which actuarial assumptions (mortality, lapse, expense) are reviewed and updated for this cohort under LDTI or IFRS 17.

attributes.name: cohort_code
attributes.description: Business-assigned unique code identifying the cohort for reporting and reference purposes. Used in actuarial systems and financial statements.

attributes.name: cohort_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the cohort for business user identification and reporting.

attributes.name: cohort_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of the cohort: active (still issuing new policies), closed (no new issues but policies in force), runoff (winding down), or fully_matured (all policies terminated or matured).

attributes.name: cohort_type
attributes.description: Classification of the cohort grouping methodology: annual (LDTI annual cohort), portfolio (IFRS 17 portfolio), group (IFRS 17 group of insurance contracts), or contract (individual contract level).

attributes.name: coverage_unit_definition
attributes.description: The definition of the coverage unit used for CSM amortization under IFRS 17 or DAC amortization under LDTI. Describes the quantity of benefits or services provided (e.g., sum assured, account value, number of policies in force).

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: The user identifier or system account that created this cohort definition record.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this cohort definition record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: current_discount_rate
attributes.description: The current period discount rate used for remeasurement of the liability under LDTI. Changes in this rate relative to the locked-in rate flow through Other Comprehensive Income (OCI). Expressed as a decimal.

attributes.name: dac_amortization_method
attributes.description: The method used to amortize Deferred Acquisition Costs for this cohort under ASC 944. LDTI requires amortization on a constant level basis over the expected life of the contracts, or in proportion to premiums, profits, or gross margins depending on product type.

attributes.name: distribution_channel
attributes.description: The primary distribution channel through which policies in this cohort were sold. Used for experience studies, profitability analysis, and commission structure alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: career_agent|independent_agent|broker|bank|direct|worksite|online — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date when this cohort definition became effective for financial reporting and actuarial valuation purposes.

attributes.name: expected_contract_life_years
attributes.description: The expected duration of contracts in this cohort from issue to maturity or termination, used for DAC amortization, reserve calculations, and cash flow projections. Expressed in years with decimal precision.

attributes.name: expense_assumption_rate
attributes.description: The assumed per-policy or per-unit expense rate for ongoing policy maintenance and administration, used in liability calculations. May be expressed as annual cost per policy or as percentage of premium.

attributes.name: geographic_market
attributes.description: The primary geographic market or jurisdiction where policies in this cohort were issued. Used for regulatory reporting, experience studies, and market segmentation analysis.

attributes.name: ifrs17_group_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standards 17 (IFRS 17) Group Code
attributes.description: The IFRS 17 group of insurance contracts identifier. Groups are subsets of portfolios divided by issue year and profitability classification (onerous, profitable, neither).

attributes.name: ifrs17_initial_recognition_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standards 17 (IFRS 17) Initial Recognition Date
attributes.description: The date when the group of insurance contracts was initially recognized under IFRS 17, establishing the cohort and locking in the initial CSM and discount rate.

attributes.name: ifrs17_portfolio_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standards 17 (IFRS 17) Portfolio Code
attributes.description: The IFRS 17 portfolio identifier to which this cohort belongs. Portfolios group insurance contracts subject to similar risks and managed together.

attributes.name: initial_csm_amount
attributes.description: The initial Contractual Service Margin calculated at initial recognition under IFRS 17. Represents the unearned profit that will be recognized as services are provided over the coverage period. Set to zero for onerous contracts.

attributes.name: initial_lfpb_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Liability for Future Policy Benefits (LFPB) Amount
attributes.description: The initial measurement of the Liability for Future Policy Benefits at cohort inception under LDTI. Represents the present value of expected future benefit payments less the present value of expected future net premiums, using the locked-in discount rate.

attributes.name: issue_quarter
attributes.description: The calendar quarter (1-4) within the issue year for more granular cohort segmentation when required by company policy or product characteristics.

attributes.name: issue_year
attributes.description: The calendar year in which policies or contracts in this cohort were issued. LDTI requires annual cohort grouping based on issue year to lock in discount rates and assumptions.

attributes.name: lapse_assumption_rate
attributes.description: The assumed annual lapse or surrender rate for policies in this cohort, used in cash flow projections and reserve calculations. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0350 for 3.50% annual lapse rate).

attributes.name: last_assumption_update_date
attributes.description: The date when actuarial assumptions for this cohort were last reviewed and updated. LDTI requires annual assumption updates at a minimum.

attributes.name: last_valuation_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which actuarial valuation was performed for this cohort. Used to track valuation currency and identify cohorts requiring remeasurement.

attributes.name: ldti_transition_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Transition Date
attributes.description: The effective date of LDTI adoption for this cohort, typically January 1, 2023 for calendar-year public companies. Used to determine transition adjustments and opening balances under the new standard.

attributes.name: locked_in_discount_rate
attributes.description: The discount rate locked in at cohort inception for LDTI liability for future policy benefits (LFPB) measurement. This rate remains constant for the cohort and is used to discount expected future cash flows. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0425 for 4.25%).

attributes.name: next_valuation_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next actuarial valuation of this cohort, typically quarterly or annually depending on reporting requirements.

attributes.name: pbr_method
attributes.description: The Principle-Based Reserving methodology applied to this cohort under NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20 or VM-21: deterministic reserve, stochastic reserve, net premium reserve, or not applicable for products not subject to PBR.

attributes.name: policy_count
attributes.description: The current number of active policies or contracts included in this cohort. Used for coverage unit calculations and experience monitoring.

attributes.name: profitability_classification
attributes.description: IFRS 17 classification of the cohort at initial recognition: onerous (expected to be loss-making), profitable (expected to generate profit), or neither (break-even). Determines initial measurement and subsequent CSM (Contractual Service Margin) treatment.

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether policies in this cohort are subject to reinsurance treaties. True if reinsurance applies, False if the cohort is retained 100% by the direct writer.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The date when this cohort definition was terminated or superseded, if applicable. Null for active cohorts.

attributes.name: total_account_value
attributes.description: The aggregate account value across all contracts in this cohort. Primary metric for annuity and universal life cohorts.

attributes.name: total_face_amount
attributes.description: The aggregate face amount or death benefit across all policies in this cohort. Key metric for life insurance cohorts and risk exposure monitoring.

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: The user identifier or system account that last modified this cohort definition record.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this cohort definition record was last modified.

products.name: assumption_detail
products.description: Typed detail records under an assumption set capturing individual assumption values by assumption type (mortality, lapse, morbidity, expense, interest rate, credibility). Stores rate values by age, duration, gender, risk class, and other segmentation dimensions. Each row is typed (mortality qx, lapse rate, expense per-policy, credited rate, etc.) and linked to its parent assumption_set. Replaces the need for separate mortality_table, lapse_assumption, disability_assumption, expense_assumption, interest_rate_assumption, and credibility_factor products while preserving full granularity. Supports PBR credibility blending, experience study updates, and pricing model calibration.

attributes.name: assumption_detail_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each assumption detail record. Primary key for the assumption detail product.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: assumption_set_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent assumption set that governs this detail record. Links this detail to its controlling assumption set for valuation runs and experience studies.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: mortality_table_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.mortality_table. Business justification: assumption_detail.mortality_table_reference (STRING) is a denormalized reference to the mortality table underlying a mortality-type assumption detail record. Adding mortality_table_id → actuarial.mort

attributes.name: prior_assumption_detail_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on assumption_detail (prior_assumption_detail_id)

attributes.name: risk_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to underwriting.risk_class. Business justification: Actuarial assumption details (mortality rates, lapse rates) are segmented by underwriting risk class per PBR/VM-20 requirements. Direct FK to the canonical risk_class definition ensures assumption seg

attributes.name: underwriting_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.underwriting_class. Business justification: assumption_detail.underwriting_class is a plain denormalized attribute. Actuarial assumptions (mortality rates, lapse rates) are set at the underwriting class level. Linking to underwriting_class enab

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this assumption detail record was formally approved by the appointed actuary or assumption governance committee.

attributes.name: assumption_basis
attributes.description: The basis or philosophy underlying this assumption detail. Indicates whether the assumption is best-estimate, conservative, prescribed by regulation, based on company experience, industry table, or a blended approach.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements, ASC 944

attributes.name: assumption_detail_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this assumption detail record. Indicates whether the assumption is in draft, actively used in valuations, superseded by a newer version, retired, or under review.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: assumption_subtype
attributes.description: Granular subtype within the assumption type. Examples: qx (mortality rate), lapse_rate, disability_incidence, per_policy_expense, credited_rate, credibility_weight. Provides additional specificity for the assumption being modeled.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: assumption_type
attributes.description: Type discriminator indicating the category of assumption this detail record represents. Determines which dimensional attributes are applicable and how the rate value should be interpreted.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements, ASC 944

attributes.name: assumption_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for this assumption detail record. Supports assumption change tracking and audit trails. Examples: v1.0, v2.1, 2024Q1.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: attained_age
attributes.description: The attained age of the insured for which this assumption rate applies. Used for age-based segmentation in mortality, lapse, and morbidity assumptions. Null if assumption is not age-dependent.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments or notes regarding this assumption detail record. Used for documenting rationale, special considerations, or assumptions about the assumption.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this assumption detail record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: credibility_factor
attributes.description: Credibility weight applied to company experience versus industry tables. Value between 0 and 1, where 1 represents full credibility to company experience. Used in PBR credibility blending calculations.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: data_source_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the data source or experience study that supports this assumption detail. Examples: experience_study_2023_Q4, SOA_2017CSO, company_mortality_study_2022, industry_lapse_benchmark.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: distribution_channel
attributes.description: Distribution channel for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: career_agent, independent_broker, direct, worksite, bank. Used for channel-based lapse and expense segmentation. Null if assumption is channel-neutral.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this assumption detail record becomes effective. Used for assumption versioning and time-based assumption changes.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: experience_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Multiplicative adjustment factor applied to base assumption rates based on company experience studies. Values greater than 1 increase the base rate; values less than 1 decrease it. Null if no experience adjustment is applied.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which this assumption detail record expires or is superseded. Null for currently active assumptions with no planned expiration.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: face_amount_band
attributes.description: Face amount band or size category for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: 0-50k, 50k-100k, 100k-250k, 250k-500k, 500k+. Used for size-based lapse and expense segmentation. Null if assumption is size-neutral.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: gender
attributes.description: Gender classification for which this assumption rate applies. M=Male, F=Female, U=Unisex or Unknown. Used for gender-based segmentation in mortality and morbidity assumptions. Null if assumption is gender-neutral.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: Geographic region or state code for which this assumption rate applies. Used for regional mortality and lapse segmentation. Null if assumption is geography-neutral.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: issue_age_band
attributes.description: Issue age band for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: 18-30, 31-40, 41-50, 51-60, 61-70, 71+. Used for issue-age-based segmentation in lapse and mortality assumptions. Null if assumption is issue-age-neutral.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this assumption detail record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: margin_percentage
attributes.description: Margin percentage added to the base assumption for conservatism or profit loading. Expressed as a percentage. Used in pricing and reserve calculations to provide cushion above best-estimate assumptions.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements, ASC 944

attributes.name: model_platform
attributes.description: The actuarial modeling platform or system that uses or generated this assumption detail. Examples: Prophet, AXIS, MoSes, GGY, internal_model. Supports traceability to modeling systems.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: mortality_improvement_scale
attributes.description: Mortality improvement scale applied to the base mortality table. Examples: Scale_G2, Scale_AA, Scale_BB, none. Applicable for mortality assumption types with projected improvements.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements, SOA Mortality Tables

attributes.name: policy_duration
attributes.description: The policy duration (years since issue) for which this assumption rate applies. Used for duration-based segmentation in lapse and mortality assumptions. Null if assumption is not duration-dependent.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: product_segment_code
attributes.description: Product segment or product type code for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: term, whole_life, universal_life, indexed_universal_life, variable_universal_life. Enables product-specific assumption calibration. Null if assumption applies across all products.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: rate_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the rate_value. Clarifies whether the value is a percentage, decimal fraction, currency amount, per-thousand rate, per-policy amount, or per-unit cost.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: rate_value
attributes.description: The numeric assumption value for this detail record. Interpretation depends on assumption_type: mortality qx, lapse percentage, expense dollar amount, interest rate percentage, credibility factor. Supports high precision for actuarial calculations.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements, ASC 944

attributes.name: regulatory_basis
attributes.description: The regulatory or accounting framework for which this assumption detail is intended. Examples: GAAP, SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS17, PBR (Principle-Based Reserving), VM-20, tax compliance.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, FASB ASC 944, IFRS 17, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: smoker_status
attributes.description: Smoking status classification for which this assumption rate applies. Used for risk-class segmentation in mortality assumptions. Null if assumption is not smoker-status-dependent.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The valuation date for which this assumption detail is calibrated or applicable. Typically aligns with the valuation run date or experience study period end date.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

products.name: mortality_table
products.description: Reference catalog of mortality tables used in actuarial valuations, pricing, and underwriting — CSO 2001, CSO 2017, VBT 2015, select and ultimate tables, smoker/non-smoker variants, and company-specific experience tables. Captures table name, table type (valuation/pricing/underwriting), gender basis, smoking class, select period, ultimate age, regulatory basis (NAIC-prescribed vs company), effective date, and superseded-by reference.

attributes.name: mortality_table_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the mortality table record. Primary key for the mortality table reference catalog.

attributes.name: base_mortality_table_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on mortality_table (base_mortality_table_id)

attributes.name: document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: Mortality tables require regulatory approval documentation filed with state DOIs and actuarial standards bodies. The existing documentation_url is denormalized; a proper FK to document enables retriev

attributes.name: experience_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the experience study that provided the empirical data foundation for this mortality table. Applicable for company-specific or industry experience-based tables. Null for prescribed regulatory tables.
attributes.references: Society of Actuaries (SOA) Experience Studies, NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Mortality tables are approved for specific product types per state insurance department filings. Each product filing specifies approved mortality tables for pricing, reserving, and nonforfeiture value

attributes.name: risk_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to underwriting.risk_class. Business justification: Mortality tables are constructed, approved, and applied for specific underwriting risk classes (e.g., preferred non-smoker, standard smoker). Direct FK from mortality_table to risk_class enables actua

attributes.name: state_regulation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.state_regulation. Business justification: State regulations mandate permissible mortality tables (e.g., CSO 2017 required by state law). mortality_table has regulatory_basis as a text field but no FK to the specific state_regulation that mand

attributes.name: underwriting_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.underwriting_class. Business justification: mortality_table.underwriting_class is a plain denormalized attribute. Mortality tables are constructed per underwriting class (preferred, standard, substandard). Actuarial table construction and PBR c

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the mortality table was formally approved for use by the appointed actuary or governance committee. Null for externally prescribed tables that do not require internal approval.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation 822 (Appointed Actuary), Society of Actuaries (SOA) Standards of Practice

attributes.name: approved_by_actuary_name
attributes.description: Full name of the appointed actuary or qualified actuary who approved the mortality table for use in the company. Required for company-specific tables; may be null for externally prescribed tables.
