attributes.name: filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.filing. Business justification: Insurance contract forms are submitted to regulators as part of a regulatory filing. The form table has filing_number STRING and filing_date DATE which are denormalized references to the filing record

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the insurance product or plan to which this form applies. Links form to product catalog.

attributes.name: plan_version_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.plan_version. Business justification: Product forms are version-specific contract documents. Each plan version may have different forms (edition_date, effective_date, expiration_date suggest versioning). Forms must match the approved vers

attributes.name: primary_predecessor_form_id
attributes.description: Reference to the previous version of this form that this edition supersedes. Enables form version lineage tracking and historical policy servicing. Nullable for initial form versions.

attributes.name: template_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.template. Business justification: Life insurance form generation uses document templates to produce state-specific policy and rider forms. The form product's document_template_path is a denormalized reference to the template entity. L

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory authority officially approved the form for use. Nullable if the form has not yet been approved or does not require approval.

attributes.name: base_form_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a base policy form that serves as the primary contract document, as opposed to a rider, endorsement, or supplementary form.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this form record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: distribution_channel
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of distribution channels authorized to use this form. Examples include career_agent, independent_agent, broker, bank, direct, worksite, online. Supports channel-specific form variations.

attributes.name: edition_date
attributes.description: The official edition or version date of the form as printed on the document. This date identifies the specific version of the form and is critical for regulatory compliance and policy administration.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this form becomes valid for use in new business issuance. Represents the start of the forms active lifecycle.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date after which this form is no longer valid for use in new business. Nullable for forms that remain active indefinitely until explicitly superseded.

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the form was officially filed with the regulatory authority for approval.

attributes.name: filing_status
attributes.description: Status of the regulatory filing for this form with state insurance departments. Tracks whether the form has been filed, approved, rejected, or is pending regulatory review.
attributes.references: NAIC System for Electronic Rate and Form Filing (SERFF)

attributes.name: form_category
attributes.description: Business category of the form indicating its primary purpose within the insurance lifecycle. Distinguishes contract documents from administrative, regulatory, marketing, compliance, or operational forms.

attributes.name: form_description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the forms purpose, content, and usage within the policy lifecycle. Provides context for underwriters, administrators, and compliance personnel.

attributes.name: form_name
attributes.description: The official title or name of the insurance form as it appears on the document and in regulatory filings.

attributes.name: form_number
attributes.description: The official form number or identifier assigned by the insurance company. This is the externally-known unique identifier used in policy documents, filings, and regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: form_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the form. Tracks the forms progression through drafting, regulatory approval, active use, and eventual retirement or supersession. attributes.name: form_type
attributes.description: Classification of the form document type. Categorizes whether this is a base policy form, application form, rider form, amendment endorsement, disclosure form, or other contract document type.

attributes.name: free_look_period_days
attributes.description: The number of days after policy delivery during which the policyholder may cancel the policy and receive a full refund, as specified on this form and required by state regulation.

attributes.name: illustration_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a policy illustration conforming to NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation must accompany this form during the sales process.
attributes.references: NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation

attributes.name: irc_7702_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Internal Revenue Code (IRC) Section 7702 Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the form and its associated product structure comply with IRC Section 7702 requirements for life insurance tax qualification. Critical for ensuring policy death benefits remain tax-free.

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 639-2 language code indicating the language in which the form is written. Supports multilingual form libraries for diverse customer populations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ENG|SPA|FRE|CHI|KOR|VIE|RUS|ARA|POR|GER — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_updated_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that last modified this form record. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this form record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: mandatory_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this form must be included with every policy issuance for the associated product, or if it is optional based on customer election or underwriting decisions.

attributes.name: mec_risk_indicator
attributes.description: Assessment of the risk that policies issued using this form may become Modified Endowment Contracts under IRC Section 7702A, which would subject withdrawals to taxation and penalties.

attributes.name: page_count
attributes.description: The number of pages in the printed or PDF version of this form. Used for document assembly and printing cost estimation.

attributes.name: print_sequence
attributes.description: The order in which this form should appear in the policy document package when multiple forms are assembled for delivery to the policyholder.

attributes.name: prospectus_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a prospectus must be delivered to the customer along with this form at point of sale, as required for variable insurance products.

attributes.name: retirement_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why this form was retired or superseded. Examples include regulatory change, product redesign, compliance update, or business strategy shift. Nullable for active forms.

attributes.name: rider_type
attributes.description: For rider forms, specifies the type of rider benefit. Examples include Accidental Death Benefit (ADB), Waiver of Premium, Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefit (GMDB), Guaranteed Minimum Income Benefit (GMIB), Guaranteed Minimum Accumulation Benefit (GMAB), Guaranteed Minimum Withdrawal Benefit (GMWB), Long-Term Care (LTC), or Disability Income (DI). products.name: plan_rider_eligibility
products.description: This association product represents the formal eligibility contract between a base plan and a rider definition in the life insurance product catalog. It captures which riders are available (or mandatory) for attachment to which base plans, with effective dating, state-level availability overrides, and sequencing rules. Each record defines one plan-rider eligibility combination as managed by the product team in the rider availability matrix. This is the operational source of truth for determining which riders can be offered at point-of-sale for a given base plan.. Existence Justification: In life insurance product management, base plans and riders have a genuine many-to-many operational relationship: a single plan (e.g., UL) can have many eligible riders (ADB, LTC, waiver of premium), and a single rider definition (e.g., ADB) can be attached to many different base plans. The business actively manages this eligibility catalog — product managers create, update, and retire plan-rider combinations with effective dating, mandatory/optional designation, and state-level availability overrides. This is a recognized operational concept in life insurance administration systems (OIPA, FAST, Majesco) called 'plan rider eligibility' or 'rider availability matrix'.

With the plan_rider_eligibility association table providing precise plan-by-plan eligibility records, this denormalized field becomes redundant and should be deprecated. The association table supersedes it with proper granularity, effective dating, and mandatory/optional designation.]
attributes.references: Product Design Specifications, Policy Administration System Configuration

products.name: plan_underwriting_eligibility
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between plan and underwriting_class defining which risk classification categories are eligible for a given product plan, under what conditions, and during what time window. It captures the plan-specific configuration of underwriting class availability including overrides to standard eligibility criteria, state-specific restrictions, and face amount overrides that exist only in the context of a specific plan-class combination. Each record links one plan to one underwriting_class and is actively managed by product actuaries and product managers during product configuration and maintenance.. Existence Justification: In life insurance product administration, a plan explicitly supports multiple underwriting classes (e.g., a Whole Life plan may offer Preferred Plus Non-Tobacco, Preferred Non-Tobacco, Standard Non-Tobacco, and Table ratings), and a single underwriting class (e.g., Standard Non-Tobacco) is available across many plans. This is not an analytical correlation — product actuaries and product managers actively configure and maintain which underwriting classes are eligible for each plan, with plan-specific overrides for face amount limits, eligibility criteria, and effective dates. The business recognizes this as 'Plan Underwriting Eligibility' or 'Risk Class Availability' and it is managed as a distinct configuration entity in product administration systems.

attributes.business_glossary_term: Plan Underwriting Eligibility - Plan Underwriting Eligibility Id
attributes.description: Primary key for the plan_underwriting_eligibility association

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the product plan for which this underwriting class eligibility is configured.

attributes.name: underwriting_class_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plan Underwriting Eligibility - Underwriting Class Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the underwriting risk classification category that is eligible under this plan configuration.

attributes.name: applicable_product_lines
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of product line codes or categories where this underwriting class is available (e.g., WL, UL, IUL, VUL, YRT, DI). Some classes may be restricted to specific product types based on underwriting complexity or reinsurance treaty terms. With the plan_underwriting_eligibility association table in place, the proper relational path exists and this field becomes redundant and should be deprecated. The association table provides a normalized, queryable, and historically accurate representation of which plans each underwriting class applies to.]
attributes.references: Product Filing Documents, Reinsurance Treaty Schedules, Company Product Catalog

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this underwriting class becomes available for new business under this specific plan. May differ from both the plan effective date and the underwriting class effective date, allowing plan-class combinations to be activated independently.

attributes.name: eligibility_override_criteria
attributes.description: Plan-specific override to the standard underwriting class eligibility criteria defined on the underwriting_class record. Captures additional or modified health, lifestyle, or risk requirements that apply only when this class is used with this plan. Null if no override applies.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which this underwriting class is no longer available for new business under this specific plan. Null indicates no scheduled expiration. Enables plan-level retirement of specific risk classes without retiring the class globally.

attributes.name: minimum_face_amount_override
attributes.description: Plan-specific minimum death benefit face amount required to qualify for this underwriting class under this plan. Overrides the class-level face_amount_minimum when set. Null if the class-level default applies without modification.

attributes.name: state_specific_restrictions
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of two-letter state codes where this plan-class combination is restricted or prohibited, beyond the general state approvals on either the plan or the underwriting class. Captures regulatory filing outcomes specific to this combination.

domains.name: compliance
domains.description: Governs regulatory compliance obligations across all jurisdictions — NAIC, state DOI filings, SEC/FINRA for variable products, IRS 7702/72 tax compliance, AML/BSA/KYC (FinCEN), HIPAA privacy, SOX controls, DOL fiduciary (ERISA), and ORSA/ERM reporting. Owns regulatory filing calendars, market conduct examination records, suitability reviews, examination findings, remediation tracking, compliance attestation workflows, and compliance training records.

products.name: regulatory_obligation
products.description: Master registry of all regulatory obligations, filing deadlines, and compliance calendar entries applicable to Life Insurance operations across all jurisdictions. Each obligation captures the governing body, regulation citation, effective date, applicability scope (product lines, states), compliance owner, filing frequency (annual, quarterly, monthly, ad hoc), statutory due date, internal preparation deadline, grace period, escalation thresholds, responsible department, and renewal cycle. Serves as the single authoritative source for what must be done, by whom, and by when — functioning as both the obligation registry and the enterprise compliance calendar for proactive deadline management.

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each regulatory obligation record in the master compliance registry. Serves as the primary key for all downstream joins and compliance tracking workflows.
attributes.references: NAIC Data Standards; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.legal_entity. Business justification: Regulatory obligations apply to specific legal entities based on domicile state, licensed jurisdictions, lines of business. Obligation tracking must be entity-specific for compliance management.

attributes.name: state_regulation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.state_regulation. Business justification: A regulatory_obligation implements or is governed by a specific state_regulation. This FK establishes the relationship between the obligation and the state-specific regulatory requirement it fulfills.

attributes.name: aml_bsa_relevance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Anti-Money Laundering / Bank Secrecy Act (AML/BSA) Relevance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is related to AML/BSA compliance programs, including KYC, Suspicious Activity Reports (SAR), Currency Transaction Reports (CTR), or FinCEN program requirements. Drives routing to the AML compliance team.
attributes.references: FinCEN 31 CFR Part 1010; Bank Secrecy Act; USA PATRIOT Act Section 326

attributes.name: applicable_product_lines
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of insurance product lines to which this obligation applies (e.g., 'WL|UL|IUL|VUL|FIA|SPIA|LTC|DI'). Null or 'ALL' for enterprise-wide obligations. Enables scoping of compliance activities to relevant business units and product portfolios.
attributes.references: NAIC Product Line Classifications; SEC Variable Product Registration; IRS IRC Section 7702

attributes.name: applicable_states
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of US state or territory codes (2-letter USPS abbreviations) where this obligation applies (e.g., 'CA|NY|TX|FL'). Null or 'ALL' for federal obligations applicable in all jurisdictions. Used to scope market conduct and state DOI filing requirements.
attributes.references: NAIC; State Departments of Insurance (all 50 US states plus territories)

attributes.name: compliance_domain
attributes.description: Primary compliance program domain to which this obligation belongs. Drives assignment to the appropriate compliance team and reporting hierarchy. Examples: AML_BSA (Anti-Money Laundering/Bank Secrecy Act), KYC (Know Your Customer), HIPAA (health data privacy), SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley financial controls), ERISA_DOL (fiduciary/retirement), tax_compliance (IRS 7702/72), market_conduct (NAIC/state DOI), solvency (RBC/ORSA/ERM), suitability (FINRA), privacy (state privacy laws). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: AML_BSA|KYC|HIPAA|SOX|ERISA_DOL|tax_compliance|market_conduct|solvency|suitability|privacy — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FinCEN AML/BSA; HIPAA Privacy Rule; SOX Section 302/404; DOL ERISA; IRS IRC 7702; NAIC ORSA; FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: compliance_owner
attributes.description: Full name or employee identifier of the designated compliance officer or manager who owns accountability for this obligation. This individual is responsible for ensuring timely and accurate fulfillment and is the primary escalation contact.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; DOL ERISA Fiduciary Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this regulatory obligation record was first created in the compliance registry. Provides the audit trail entry point for the obligation lifecycle and supports SOX IT general controls documentation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this regulatory obligation first became applicable to the company. Marks the start of the compliance obligation lifecycle. Used to determine historical applicability and retroactive filing requirements.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; IRS IRC Section 7702; FASB ASC 944 LDTI Effective Date

attributes.name: escalation_contact
attributes.description: Full name or employee identifier of the senior officer or executive to whom this obligation is escalated if the internal preparation deadline is missed or a compliance risk is identified. Typically the Chief Compliance Officer or General Counsel.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC ORSA; ERM Framework

attributes.name: escalation_threshold_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days before the statutory due date at which an automated escalation alert is triggered if the obligation has not been completed. Drives the compliance calendar alert engine and executive notification workflows.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; ERM Framework

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which this regulatory obligation ceases to apply, if applicable. Null for open-ended, ongoing obligations. Populated for time-limited regulations, sunset provisions, or temporary regulatory waivers.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; IRS Temporary Regulations; SEC No-Action Letters

attributes.name: filing_frequency
attributes.description: How often this regulatory obligation must be fulfilled. Drives the compliance calendar generation logic and deadline scheduling. 'ad_hoc' = triggered by a specific business event (e.g., material change, acquisition); 'event_triggered' = triggered by a policyholder or claim event. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: annual|semi_annual|quarterly|monthly|ad_hoc|event_triggered|biennial — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC Reporting Calendar; IRS Filing Deadlines

attributes.name: filing_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the reporting or filing period covered by this obligation instance (e.g., December 31 for an annual filing). Together with filing_period_start_date, defines the data scope for the filing.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; IRS Tax Year Definitions; SEC Fiscal Year Reporting

attributes.name: filing_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the reporting or filing period covered by this obligation instance (e.g., January 1 for an annual filing). Defines the data scope for the filing and aligns with the statutory reporting period.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; IRS Tax Year Definitions; SEC Fiscal Year Reporting

attributes.name: governing_body
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory authority or governing body that mandates this obligation (e.g., NAIC, SEC, FINRA, IRS, DOL, FinCEN, FASB, State DOI — California, IAIS). Drives routing of filings and escalation contacts. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NAIC|SEC|FINRA|IRS|DOL|FinCEN|FASB|State DOI|IAIS|ACORD — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC; SEC; FINRA; IRS; DOL ERISA; FinCEN AML/BSA; FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: grace_period_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days after the statutory due date within which the obligation may still be fulfilled without incurring a penalty, as permitted by the governing body. Zero if no grace period is allowed. Used in escalation threshold calculations.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; IRS Publication 509; State DOI Filing Rules

attributes.name: hipaa_relevance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Relevance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation involves HIPAA Privacy Rule or Security Rule compliance, including protected health information (PHI) handling, breach notification, or business associate agreement requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR Part 164; HIPAA Security Rule; HITECH Act

attributes.name: internal_preparation_deadline
attributes.description: Enterprise-set internal deadline for completing all preparation, review, and approval activities prior to the statutory due date. Provides buffer time for quality review, legal sign-off, and executive attestation. Typically set 5–15 business days before the statutory due date.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: is_attestation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation requires a formal officer or executive attestation (e.g., SOX CEO/CFO certification, ORSA officer sign-off). When true, the compliance workflow must include an attestation step before submission.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC ORSA Model Regulation #505

attributes.name: is_external_filing
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation requires submission of a document or report to an external regulatory body (true) or is an internal compliance activity only (false), such as an internal audit or training completion record.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR; IRS e-file; FinCEN BSA E-Filing

attributes.name: is_material_obligation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is classified as material for SOX, ORSA, or ERM reporting purposes. Material obligations receive heightened monitoring, executive visibility, and are included in the Board-level compliance dashboard.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC ORSA Model Regulation #505; FASB ASC 944 LDTI

attributes.name: jurisdiction_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is imposed at the federal, state, multi-state, or international level. Drives routing to the appropriate legal and compliance team and determines which state DOI contacts are relevant.
attributes.references: NAIC; SEC; IRS; DOL ERISA; State Departments of Insurance; IAIS

attributes.name: last_amended_date
attributes.description: The date on which the underlying regulation or rule governing this obligation was most recently amended or updated by the governing body. Triggers a compliance review to assess whether the obligation scope, format, or deadline has changed.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation Amendment History; IRS Revenue Rulings; SEC Rule Amendments

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this regulatory obligation record was most recently modified in the compliance registry. Used to detect stale records, trigger re-review workflows, and support audit trail requirements under SOX and NAIC market conduct standards.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: ldti_relevance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Relevance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is related to FASB ASC 944-40 Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) accounting standard compliance, including updated reserve calculations, discount rate assumptions, and enhanced disclosures for long-duration insurance contracts.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944-40 LDTI; GAAP; NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: obligation_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this regulatory obligation within the enterprise compliance calendar (e.g., NAIC-ORSA-ANN, IRS-7702-QTR, SEC-N-CEN-ANN). Used as the business-facing identifier in filings, dashboards, and audit correspondence.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: obligation_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the regulatory obligation as recognized by the governing body (e.g., 'Annual ORSA Summary Report', 'Form N-CEN Annual Report', 'NAIC Risk-Based Capital Report'). Used in compliance calendars, executive dashboards, and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; SEC Reporting Requirements; IRS Publication 535

attributes.name: obligation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for compliance team annotations, regulatory guidance interpretations, special instructions, or contextual notes relevant to fulfilling this obligation. May include references to regulatory guidance letters, no-action letters, or internal legal opinions.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: obligation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the regulatory obligation within the enterprise compliance registry. 'active' = currently enforceable; 'suspended' = temporarily waived by regulator; 'retired' = no longer applicable; 'pending_effective' = enacted but not yet in force; 'under_review' = applicability being assessed by compliance team.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: obligation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the compliance obligation. 'filing' = periodic regulatory report submission; 'examination' = market conduct or financial exam; 'attestation' = SOX/officer certification; 'disclosure' = required customer or public disclosure; 'training' = mandatory compliance training; 'audit' = internal or external audit; 'notification' = event-triggered regulatory notice; 'registration' = product or entity registration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: filing|examination|attestation|disclosure|training|audit|notification|registration — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 302/404; HIPAA Privacy Rule

attributes.name: orsa_erm_relevance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Own Risk and Solvency Assessment / Enterprise Risk Management (ORSA/ERM) Relevance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is part of the ORSA or ERM reporting framework, including the annual ORSA Summary Report submitted to state regulators. Used to scope the ERM compliance calendar and Board risk reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Model Regulation #505; IAIS Insurance Core Principles; ERM Framework

attributes.name: pbr_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is related to NAIC Principle-Based Reserving (PBR) compliance, including VM-20 (life insurance reserves), VM-21 (variable annuity reserves), and VM-31 (PBR actuarial report) requirements. Used to scope actuarial compliance activities.
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20; NAIC Valuation Manual VM-21; NAIC Valuation Manual VM-31; PBR

attributes.name: penalty_amount_usd
attributes.description: Maximum or standard monetary penalty in US dollars that may be assessed for non-compliance with this obligation. Used in risk quantification, ERM reporting, and prioritization of compliance resources. Null if penalty is non-monetary (e.g., license suspension).
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; IRS Penalty Provisions; SEC Enforcement Actions; State DOI Penalty Schedules

attributes.name: penalty_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the regulatory penalties, fines, or sanctions that may be imposed for non-compliance or late filing (e.g., '$100 per day late fee', 'license suspension', 'cease and desist order'). Informs risk prioritization and escalation urgency.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; IRS Penalty Provisions; SEC Enforcement Actions; State DOI Penalty Schedules

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Enterprise-assigned priority classification for this obligation based on regulatory risk, penalty severity, and business impact. 'critical' = Board-level visibility, zero tolerance for non-compliance; 'high' = executive escalation required if at risk; 'medium' = standard compliance monitoring; 'low' = routine administrative obligation.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Model Regulation #505; ERM Framework; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: rbc_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this obligation is directly related to NAIC Risk-Based Capital (RBC) reporting or solvency compliance. Used to prioritize obligations in the actuarial and finance compliance calendar and to scope RBC-related remediation activities.
attributes.references: NAIC Risk-Based Capital (RBC) Instructions; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: regulation_citation
attributes.description: Formal legal or regulatory citation for the rule or statute that creates this obligation (e.g., 'IRC Section 7702', 'NAIC Model Regulation #820', 'ERISA Section 404', 'ASC 944-40 LDTI', 'FinCEN 31 CFR Part 1010'). Enables precise traceability to source regulation for audit and legal review.
attributes.references: IRS IRC Section 7702; NAIC Model Regulations; DOL ERISA; FASB ASC 944; FinCEN 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: renewal_cycle_months
attributes.description: Number of months in the renewal or recurrence cycle for this obligation (e.g., 12 for annual, 3 for quarterly, 1 for monthly). Used by the compliance calendar engine to auto-generate future obligation instances. Null for one-time or event-triggered obligations.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; IRS Filing Deadlines; SEC Reporting Calendar

attributes.name: responsible_department
attributes.description: Name of the internal department or business unit primarily responsible for fulfilling this obligation (e.g., 'Actuarial', 'Legal & Compliance', 'Finance', 'Tax', 'Operations', 'Investment Management'). Used for workload assignment and escalation routing.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system of record from which this obligation record originates or is primarily managed (e.g., 'Compliance Calendar System', 'Policy Administration System', 'Actuarial Valuation System'). Supports data lineage and ETL traceability in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; SOX Section 404 IT Controls

attributes.name: statutory_due_date
attributes.description: The legally mandated deadline by which this obligation must be fulfilled as specified by the governing body or regulation. For recurring obligations, this represents the due date for the current or next filing period. Failure to meet this date may result in regulatory penalties.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; IRS Filing Deadlines; SEC Reporting Calendar; DOL ERISA Filing Deadlines

attributes.name: submission_channel
attributes.description: The required or preferred method by which this obligation must be submitted to the governing body. 'electronic' = NAIC SERFF or similar; 'portal' = regulator-specific web portal (e.g., SEC EDGAR, IRS e-file); 'api' = machine-to-machine submission; 'paper' = physical mailing.
attributes.references: NAIC SERFF; SEC EDGAR; IRS e-file; FinCEN BSA E-Filing System

attributes.name: submission_format
attributes.description: The required data format or form number for the filing submission (e.g., 'NAIC Annual Statement Blank', 'Form N-CEN', 'Form 5500', 'SAR FinCEN 111', 'ACORD XML'). Ensures the compliance team prepares the filing in the correct format required by the governing body.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC Form N-CEN; DOL Form 5500; FinCEN SAR; ACORD Data Standards

products.name: regulatory_filing
products.description: Transactional record of every regulatory filing submitted to governing bodies — NAIC annual/quarterly statements, state DOI market conduct filings, SEC Form N-4/N-6 for variable products, FINRA filings, IRS Form 1099-R/5498, FinCEN SAR/CTR filings, ORSA reports, ERISA Form 5500 filings, and all other statutory submissions. Captures filing type, jurisdiction, submission date, due date, filing status (draft, submitted, accepted, rejected), filing period, preparer, approver, and submission confirmation reference. For ORSA filings: includes risk categories assessed, capital adequacy conclusion, stress test scenarios, board approval date, and lead state designation. For ERISA filings: includes plan sponsor, plan type (group life, 401k annuity, pension), fiduciary designation, prohibited transaction exemption (PTE) references, and DOL filing date. Serves as the single transactional record for all regulatory submissions regardless of filing type or governing body.

attributes.name: aml_transaction_type
attributes.description: For FinCEN filings, identifies whether this is a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) or Currency Transaction Report (CTR). Applicable only to FinCEN/BSA filings. Null for non-AML filing types. Supports AML/BSA compliance tracking.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the designated approver formally signed off on the filing prior to submission. Required for SOX internal control documentation and NAIC officer certification.

attributes.description: Full name of the officer or compliance official who approved the filing. Retained for audit trail and regulatory examination purposes.

attributes.name: board_approval_date

attributes.name: capital_adequacy_conclusion

attributes.name: confirmation_reference
attributes.description: The acknowledgment or confirmation number returned by the governing body's filing system upon successful receipt of the submission (e.g., NAIC confirmation number, SEC accession number, DOL EFAST2 confirmation, FinCEN BSA tracking number). Serves as the authoritative proof of submission.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR Accession Number; DOL EFAST2; FinCEN BSA E-Filing

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this regulatory filing record was first created in the compliance system. Provides the audit trail entry point for the filing lifecycle. Aligns with SOX internal control documentation requirements.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for any monetary amounts reported in this filing (e.g., 'USD'). Primarily USD for domestic US regulatory filings. Required when penalty_amount or other monetary fields are populated.

attributes.name: days_late

attributes.name: due_date

Used to calculate timeliness, trigger escalation workflows, and assess late-filing penalties. Derived from the regulatory calendar for the applicable filing type and jurisdiction.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2; IRS Publication 1220

attributes.name: erisa_plan_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) Plan Type
attributes.description: Classification of the ERISA-covered plan reported in this DOL Form 5500 filing (e.g., group life, 401k annuity, pension, welfare). Applicable only to ERISA filings. Null for non-ERISA filing types.
attributes.references: DOL ERISA; DOL Form 5500 Instructions; IRC Section 401

attributes.name: fiduciary_designation
attributes.description: Name or role of the designated fiduciary responsible for the ERISA plan covered by this filing. Required for DOL Form 5500 and DOL fiduciary compliance under ERISA. Null for non-ERISA filing types.
attributes.references: DOL ERISA Section 3(21); DOL Form 5500 Instructions

attributes.name: filing_channel
attributes.description: The transmission method used to submit the filing to the governing body (e.g., electronic via NAIC SERFF, SEC EDGAR, DOL EFAST2, FinCEN BSA E-Filing portal, or paper submission). Relevant for audit trail and submission confirmation tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC SERFF; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2; FinCEN BSA E-Filing

attributes.name: filing_form_name
attributes.description: The official name or designation of the regulatory form used for this filing (e.g., 'NAIC Life/Health Annual Statement', 'SEC Form N-4', 'IRS Form 1099-R', 'FinCEN Form 112 CTR', 'DOL Form 5500', 'ORSA Summary Report'). Provides precise identification of the statutory instrument.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC Forms N-4/N-6; IRS Publication 1220; FinCEN Form 112; DOL Form 5500

attributes.name: filing_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable reference number assigned to the filing — either generated internally or assigned by the receiving regulatory body upon submission (e.g., NAIC filing reference, SEC accession number, DOL confirmation number). Used for tracking and correspondence with regulators.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR Filing System; DOL EFAST2

attributes.name: filing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the regulatory filing submission. Tracks progression from internal preparation (draft) through submission to the regulator and final disposition (accepted, rejected, withdrawn). Drives compliance workflow and remediation tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2; FinCEN BSA E-Filing

attributes.name: filing_system_source
attributes.description: Name of the internal operational system or platform from which the filing data was sourced or generated (e.g., 'Policy Administration System', 'Actuarial Valuation System', 'Claims Management System'). Supports data lineage and ETL traceability.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: filing_version
attributes.description: Version or amendment number of this filing submission (e.g., 'original', 'amendment_1', 'corrected'). Tracks whether this is the initial submission or a subsequent amendment/correction filed with the governing body.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR Amendment Rules; IRS Publication 1220

attributes.name: is_amended
attributes.description: Indicates whether this filing is an amendment or correction to a previously submitted filing. True if this is an amended submission; False if this is the original filing. Used to distinguish original from corrected statutory submissions.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR Amendment Rules; IRS Publication 1220

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this regulatory filing record was most recently modified in the compliance system. Tracks the most recent status change, amendment, or data correction. Supports audit trail and SOX change management controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: late_filing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this filing was submitted after the statutory due date. True if submission_date exceeds due_date; False if filed on time. Used for compliance monitoring, penalty assessment, and regulatory examination preparation.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR Late Filing Rules; DOL EFAST2; IRS Publication 1220

attributes.name: lead_state_code
attributes.description: Two-character US state code identifying the lead state regulator for ORSA filings and multi-state regulatory submissions. The lead state coordinates review among all states where the insurer is licensed. Applicable primarily to ORSA and group-level filings.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual; NAIC Group Supervision Framework

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for compliance officers to record supplemental context, internal commentary, regulator correspondence notes, or remediation instructions related to this filing. Not transmitted to the regulator; for internal compliance workflow use only.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: orsa_risk_categories
attributes.business_glossary_term: Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) Risk Categories
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of risk categories assessed in the ORSA filing (e.g., 'insurance_risk, market_risk, credit_risk, operational_risk, liquidity_risk'). Applicable only to ORSA filings. Null for non-ORSA filing types. Supports ERM and ORSA reporting requirements.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual; IAIS Insurance Core Principles

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: Monetary penalty assessed by the governing body for late or deficient filing, expressed in USD. Null if no penalty was assessed. Used for financial reporting, regulatory expense tracking, and SOX control monitoring.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC Late Filing Penalties; DOL ERISA Penalty Rules; IRS Penalty Provisions

attributes.name: plan_sponsor_name
attributes.description: Name of the employer or organization sponsoring the retirement or group benefit plan covered by this ERISA filing (DOL Form 5500). Applicable only to ERISA filings. Null for non-ERISA filing types.
attributes.references: DOL ERISA Section 103; DOL Form 5500 Instructions

attributes.name: preparer_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual responsible for preparing the regulatory filing. Retained for audit trail and regulatory examination purposes even if the employee record changes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: pte_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier for any Prohibited Transaction Exemption (PTE) cited in the ERISA filing (e.g., PTE 84-24, PTE 2020-02). Applicable to ERISA filings where prohibited transaction exemptions are claimed. Null for non-ERISA filing types.
attributes.references: DOL ERISA Section 408; DOL PTE 84-24; DOL PTE 2020-02

attributes.name: rejection_date
attributes.description: The date on which the governing body formally rejected the filing. Populated only when filing_status is 'rejected'. Triggers remediation workflow and resubmission tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Textual description or regulator-provided code explaining why the filing was rejected. Populated when filing_status is 'rejected'. Used to drive remediation actions and resubmission preparation.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2

attributes.name: stress_test_scenarios
attributes.description: Description or comma-separated list of stress test scenarios included in the ORSA or actuarial filing (e.g., 'interest_rate_shock, pandemic_mortality, equity_market_decline'). Applicable to ORSA and actuarial valuation filings. Null for non-ORSA filing types.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual; FASB ASC 944; LDTI

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The actual calendar date on which the filing was transmitted to the governing body. Compared against due_date to determine timeliness and potential late-filing exposure. Populated upon successful transmission.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2; FinCEN BSA E-Filing

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the filing was electronically transmitted to the governing body. Provides audit-grade evidence of timely submission, particularly for filings with intraday deadlines (e.g., FinCEN CTR 15-day rule).
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA E-Filing; SEC EDGAR; DOL EFAST2

products.name: market_conduct_exam
products.description: Comprehensive record of state DOI market conduct examinations, their associated findings, and finding-level detail. Captures examination type (routine, targeted, multi-state), initiating state DOI, scope, lead examiner, examination period, status, and outcome. Includes embedded finding records: finding description, regulatory citation violated, severity classification (critical, major, minor), affected policy counts, examiner recommendations, company response, finding status (open, disputed, remediated, closed), and corrective action deadlines. Supports the full examination lifecycle from notification through finding closure and repeat-finding trend analysis across examination cycles.

attributes.name: market_conduct_exam_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each market conduct examination record in the compliance system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: agency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agent.agency. Business justification: Market conduct exams routinely examine agency-level distribution practices, sales supervision, and complaint handling. Regulators scope exams to specific agencies. Linking market_conduct_exam to agenc

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Exam response costs (legal counsel, document production, staff time, remediation) are significant and tracked by cost center for budget variance analysis and management accountability. Required for fi

attributes.name: exam_report_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: Market conduct exams produce official exam reports (draft and final) stored in the document system. Compliance officers need to link the exam record to its primary report document for regulatory respo

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policy.in_force_policy. Business justification: Market conduct exams sample specific policies for review of sales practices, underwriting, claims, and policy administration. Linking exam to sampled policies enables tracking which policies were exam

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Market conduct exams result in monetary penalties and restitution amounts that must be accrued as journal entries. Insurance finance teams book penalty accruals and restitution liabilities when exam o

attributes.name: jurisdiction_license_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.jurisdiction_license. Business justification: A market conduct exam is conducted within a specific jurisdiction where the company holds a Certificate of Authority. Linking market_conduct_exam to jurisdiction_license enables tracking which license

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.legal_entity. Business justification: Market conduct exams are conducted against specific legal entities. Exam scope, findings, and penalties are entity-specific for regulatory accountability and financial statement impact.

attributes.name: portfolio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.portfolio. Business justification: Market conduct exams review investment practices, variable product sales, separate account management, and portfolio compliance. Real business process: regulatory examination, investment compliance re

attributes.name: producer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agent.producer. Business justification: Market conduct exams are frequently initiated due to specific producer conduct complaints (churning, misrepresentation, unsuitable sales). Regulators and compliance teams need to link exams to the imp

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: A market conduct examination is triggered by or conducted in fulfillment of a specific regulatory obligation (e.g., NAIC market conduct annual statement, state DOI examination cycle). Linking market_c

attributes.name: state_regulation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.state_regulation. Business justification: A market conduct exam is conducted under the authority of specific state insurance regulations. Adding state_regulation_id normalizes the governing regulatory framework. initiating_state_code is retai

attributes.name: appeal_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the company has filed a formal appeal or objection to the examination findings or enforcement action. True if an appeal has been filed; False otherwise. Triggers legal hold and appeal tracking workflow.
attributes.references: State DOI Administrative Procedures; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: appeal_filed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the company formally filed its appeal or objection with the state DOI or administrative tribunal. Null if no appeal has been filed. Used to track appeal timelines and regulatory response deadlines.
attributes.references: State DOI Administrative Procedures; Administrative Procedures Act

attributes.name: appeal_resolution
attributes.description: Outcome of the company's formal appeal of examination findings or enforcement action. Null if no appeal was filed or appeal is still pending. Values: pending (appeal filed, awaiting decision), upheld (original findings confirmed), partially_upheld (some findings modified), overturned (findings reversed), withdrawn (company withdrew appeal).
attributes.references: State DOI Administrative Procedures; Administrative Procedures Act

attributes.name: cap_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the state DOI formally approved the company's submitted Corrective Action Plan (CAP). Null if the CAP has not yet been approved or is not required. Marks the start of the formal remediation execution period.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Enforcement Orders

attributes.name: cap_submission_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the company submitted its Corrective Action Plan (CAP) to the state DOI. Null if the CAP has not yet been submitted. Used to track timeliness of regulatory response and compliance with DOI deadlines.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Enforcement Orders

attributes.name: cap_submission_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) Submission Due Date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the company must submit its Corrective Action Plan (CAP) to the state DOI. Null if no CAP is required. Triggers internal compliance workflow and executive escalation if approaching without submission.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Enforcement Orders

attributes.name: company_exam_coordinator
attributes.description: Full name of the internal company employee designated as the primary point of contact and coordinator for this market conduct examination. Responsible for document production, examiner liaison, and internal response coordination.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; Internal Compliance Policy

attributes.name: company_legal_counsel
attributes.description: Name of the internal or external legal counsel assigned to advise the company during the market conduct examination. Responsible for legal strategy, response drafting, and appeal proceedings if applicable.
attributes.references: State DOI Examination Procedures; Internal Legal Policy

attributes.name: company_response_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the company must submit its formal written response to the draft examination report findings. Calculated from the draft report issuance date per state DOI requirements. Failure to respond by this date may result in findings being finalized without company input.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Procedures

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the state DOI has required the company to submit a formal Corrective Action Plan (CAP) as a result of examination findings. True if a CAP is required; False if no formal plan is mandated. Drives the corrective action tracking workflow.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Enforcement Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market conduct examination record was first created in the compliance management system. Represents the system-of-record audit trail creation event. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: critical_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of examination findings classified as critical severity — representing systemic violations, significant consumer harm, or material regulatory non-compliance requiring immediate corrective action. Supports executive reporting and regulatory escalation tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Enforcement Guidelines

attributes.name: draft_report_date
attributes.description: Date on which the state DOI issued the preliminary draft examination report to the company for review and response. Initiates the company's formal response period, which is typically 30 days under NAIC standards.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Procedures

attributes.name: exam_close_date
attributes.description: Date on which the state DOI formally closed the examination after confirming all findings have been remediated or resolved. Represents the end of the examination lifecycle. Null if the examination is still open.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Procedures

attributes.name: exam_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for internal compliance team notes regarding the examination, including context about regulatory relationships, strategic considerations, unusual circumstances, or coordination with other regulatory matters. Not shared with the DOI.

attributes.name: exam_number
attributes.description: Externally-assigned examination reference number issued by the initiating state Department of Insurance (DOI). Used for correspondence, filings, and cross-referencing with the regulator. Format varies by state DOI.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Filing Requirements

attributes.name: exam_outcome
attributes.description: Regulatory outcome or enforcement action resulting from the completed examination. Captures the most severe action taken: no_action (no violations found or all minor), corrective_action_plan (formal CAP required), consent_order (negotiated regulatory agreement), cease_and_desist (order to stop specific practices), license_suspension (temporary license action), monetary_penalty (fine assessed), restitution_ordered (consumer repayment required), multi_action (multiple enforcement actions). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: no_action|corrective_action_plan|consent_order|cease_and_desist|license_suspension|monetary_penalty|restitution_ordered|multi_action — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Enforcement Guidelines

attributes.name: exam_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the business activity review period covered by the examination. Defines the latest date of company records and transactions subject to examiner review.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Notice

attributes.name: exam_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the business activity review period covered by the examination. Defines the earliest date of company records and transactions subject to examiner review. Typically spans 3-5 years of prior business activity.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Notice

attributes.name: exam_scope
attributes.description: Narrative description of the business areas, product lines, and practices subject to review in this examination. May reference specific lines of business (life, annuity, disability), functional areas (claims, underwriting, sales, billing), or regulatory concerns (suitability, AML, HIPAA). Derived from the DOI examination notice.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Regulation Handbook; State DOI Examination Notice

attributes.name: exam_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the market conduct examination from initial notification through final closure. Tracks the examination workflow stage: notification_received (DOI notice received), in_progress (active examination underway), draft_report (preliminary findings issued), response_pending (company response to draft due), final_report (final examination report issued), closed (all findings resolved), appealed (company has filed a formal appeal). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: notification_received|in_progress|draft_report|response_pending|final_report|closed|appealed — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Procedures

attributes.name: exam_type
attributes.description: Classification of the market conduct examination by its scope and trigger. Routine examinations are scheduled periodic reviews; targeted examinations focus on specific business practices; multi-state examinations are coordinated across multiple state DOIs; for-cause examinations are triggered by complaints or regulatory concerns; desk examinations are conducted remotely; market analysis examinations are data-driven reviews.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards (MCES); NAIC Market Regulation Handbook

attributes.name: final_report_date
attributes.description: Date on which the state DOI issued the final examination report incorporating company responses and examiner determinations. This is the official regulatory record of examination findings and required corrective actions.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Procedures

attributes.name: functional_areas_examined
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of business functional areas reviewed during the examination (e.g., 'claims_adjudication, policy_servicing, sales_practices, underwriting, billing, complaint_handling, anti_money_laundering'). Supports gap analysis and remediation planning.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Regulation Handbook; NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS)

attributes.name: initiating_state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter USPS state abbreviation identifying the lead state Department of Insurance that initiated and is conducting the market conduct examination. For multi-state examinations, this is the lead state coordinating the review.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; USPS State Abbreviation Standard

attributes.name: lead_examiner_contact
attributes.description: Email address or phone number of the state DOI lead examiner for official examination correspondence. Used by the company's compliance team to coordinate document requests, schedule interviews, and submit responses.

attributes.name: lead_examiner_name
attributes.description: Full name of the state DOI lead examiner assigned to conduct and oversee the market conduct examination. Used for correspondence, scheduling, and examination record attribution. This is a regulatory contact, not a company employee.

attributes.name: lines_of_business
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of insurance product lines included in the examination scope (e.g., 'whole_life, term_life, annuity, disability_income, long_term_care'). Aligns with NAIC line-of-business classifications. Supports product-level finding analysis and trend reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Line of Business Classifications; NAIC Market Regulation Handbook

attributes.name: major_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of examination findings classified as major severity — representing significant but non-systemic violations requiring formal corrective action plans. Supports prioritization of remediation resources.

attributes.name: minor_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of examination findings classified as minor severity — representing isolated or technical violations with limited consumer impact. Typically addressed through process improvements rather than formal corrective action plans.

attributes.name: monetary_penalty_amount
attributes.description: Total monetary penalty or fine assessed by the state DOI as a result of this examination, expressed in US dollars. Null if no monetary penalty was assessed. Supports financial exposure tracking, SOX controls, and regulatory liability reporting. Classified as confidential due to business-sensitive financial exposure.
attributes.references: State DOI Enforcement Orders; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the company received official written notification from the state Department of Insurance of the upcoming or initiated market conduct examination. Triggers internal response timelines and document preservation obligations.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI Examination Notice

attributes.name: onsite_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the active on-site (or remote desk) examination phase concluded and examiners departed or ceased active record review. Marks the transition to report drafting phase.

attributes.name: onsite_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which examiners physically arrived at company premises (or commenced remote access for desk examinations) to begin active review of records and interviews. Null for market analysis examinations that are entirely data-driven.

attributes.name: participating_states
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of two-letter USPS state abbreviations for all states participating in a multi-state market conduct examination, excluding the initiating state. Null or empty for single-state examinations. Supports multi-state coordination tracking per NAIC protocols.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; NAIC Multi-State Examination Protocol

attributes.name: prior_exam_reference
attributes.description: Examination number of the prior market conduct examination that this examination follows up on, if applicable. Null if this is not a repeat examination. Enables linkage between examination cycles for repeat-finding trend analysis.

attributes.name: repeat_exam_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this examination is a follow-up or repeat examination triggered by unresolved findings from a prior examination cycle. True if this is a repeat examination; False if it is an initial examination. Critical for repeat-finding trend analysis and regulatory escalation risk assessment.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; NAIC Market Regulation Handbook

attributes.name: restitution_amount
attributes.description: Total amount of consumer restitution ordered by the state DOI as a result of examination findings, expressed in US dollars. Represents payments owed to policyholders harmed by identified violations. Null if no restitution was ordered. Classified as confidential due to business-sensitive financial exposure.
attributes.references: State DOI Enforcement Orders; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: total_findings_count
attributes.description: Total number of distinct examination findings identified across all severity levels in this examination. Provides a high-level measure of examination outcome severity and supports trend analysis across examination cycles.

attributes.name: total_policies_examined
attributes.description: Total number of individual policy or contract records reviewed by examiners during the examination. Represents the full sample size across all functional areas and lines of business examined. Used to calculate error rates and assess statistical significance of findings.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; NAIC Market Regulation Handbook

attributes.name: total_policies_with_findings
attributes.description: Total number of policy or contract records in which at least one examination finding was identified. Used to calculate the overall error rate (policies with findings / total policies examined) and assess the breadth of non-compliance.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market conduct examination record was most recently modified in the compliance management system. Supports audit trail, change detection, and incremental ETL processing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Policy

products.name: exam_finding
products.description: Individual finding or deficiency identified during a market conduct examination, regulatory audit, or internal compliance review. Captures finding description, regulatory citation violated, severity classification (critical, major, minor), affected business process, number of impacted policies or transactions, examiner recommendation, company response, and finding status (open, disputed, remediated, closed). Supports remediation tracking and repeat-finding analysis.

attributes.name: exam_finding_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual finding or deficiency identified during a market conduct examination, regulatory audit, or internal compliance review.

attributes.name: actual_penalty_amount
attributes.description: Actual monetary penalty or fine levied by the regulatory authority as a result of this finding (USD). Null if no penalty was assessed.
attributes.references: NAIC; State DOI; SEC; FINRA; FinCEN; IRS

attributes.name: actual_remediation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the company completed all corrective actions and the finding was substantively remediated, used to measure remediation cycle time against target.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 404

attributes.description: The core business process or operational area implicated by the finding (e.g., Policy Underwriting and Risk Assessment, Premium Billing and Collection, Claims Adjudication and Settlement, Annuity Contract Administration, Agent and Broker Commission Management). attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; ACORD

attributes.description: The primary data domain impacted by the finding, used to route remediation ownership and cross-domain impact analysis. attributes.name: aml_bsa_related
attributes.business_glossary_term: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) Related Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this finding relates to AML/BSA compliance obligations, including KYC deficiencies, suspicious activity reporting failures, or FinCEN regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML; NAIC AML Model Regulation; USA PATRIOT Act

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the examining authority or internal compliance function formally accepted the remediation and closed the finding.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; State DOI

attributes.name: company_response
attributes.description: Official company response to the finding, including acceptance, dispute rationale, or proposed corrective action plan submitted to the examining authority.
attributes.references: NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: compliance_attestation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal compliance attestation from a senior officer or compliance officer is required to close this finding, as mandated by the examining authority or internal governance policy.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; NAIC Corporate Governance Model Regulation; ORSA
