attributes.name: disclosure_provided_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether all required regulatory disclosures (e.g., NAIC Buyer's Guide, product prospectus for variable products, fee disclosure) were provided to the client prior to or at the time of sale.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 7; SEC Rule 10b-5; FINRA Rule 2210

attributes.name: existing_insurance_coverage
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client has existing life insurance or annuity coverage at the time of the suitability review, relevant for replacement analysis and concentration assessment.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6A; NAIC Replacement Model Regulation #613

attributes.name: finra_reg_bi_applicable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether SEC Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI) applies to this transaction, typically for variable product sales through registered broker-dealers.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI) effective June 30, 2020; FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: investment_amount
attributes.description: The premium or investment amount in USD placed into the recommended product at the time of sale. Used to assess concentration risk relative to the client's total liquid net worth.

attributes.name: investment_objective
attributes.description: Client's primary investment objective as stated on the suitability questionnaire. Drives product recommendation alignment analysis.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6A; FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: investment_time_horizon
attributes.description: Client's stated investment time horizon: short_term (under 3 years), medium_term (3–10 years), long_term (over 10 years). Must be compatible with product surrender charge period.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6A; FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: is_1035_exchange
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction involves a tax-free 1035 exchange of an existing insurance or annuity contract, requiring additional suitability analysis of surrender charges, tax implications, and benefit comparisons.
attributes.references: IRC Section 1035 (Tax-Free Insurance Policy Exchange); IRS Publication 575

attributes.name: is_replacement
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sale involves the replacement of an existing life insurance policy or annuity contract, triggering additional disclosure and suitability requirements under NAIC Model Regulation #613.
attributes.references: NAIC Life Insurance Replacement Model Regulation #613; State DOI replacement regulations

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code of the jurisdiction in which the sale transaction occurred, determining applicable state DOI suitability rules and disclosure requirements.
attributes.references: State Departments of Insurance (all 50 US states); NAIC Model Regulation #275

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this suitability review record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements and change tracking for regulatory examination purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Model Regulation #275; State DOI market conduct examination standards

attributes.name: liquid_net_worth
attributes.description: Client's liquid net worth in USD (readily accessible assets excluding illiquid holdings such as real estate and retirement accounts) at the time of review. Critical for assessing ability to meet surrender charges and liquidity needs.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6A; DOL Fiduciary Rule

attributes.name: net_worth
attributes.description: Client's total net worth in USD (assets minus liabilities) at the time of the suitability review, as self-reported. Used to evaluate financial capacity and product suitability relative to overall wealth.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6A; FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client elected to proceed with the transaction despite a 'not_suitable' or 'conditionally_suitable' determination, exercising their right to override the recommendation. Requires documented client acknowledgment.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6C; State DOI regulations

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: Documented reason provided by the client for proceeding with the transaction despite a non-suitable or conditional determination. Required when override_flag is True.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6C; State DOI regulations

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: The type of insurance or annuity product recommended. Uses industry-standard abbreviations: FIA (Fixed Indexed Annuity), VUL (Variable Universal Life), UL (Universal Life), WL (Whole Life), IUL (Indexed Universal Life), SPIA (Single Premium Immediate Annuity), DI (Disability Income), LTC (Long-Term Care), term (Term Life). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FIA|VUL|UL|WL|IUL|SPIA|DI|LTC|term|GMWB|GMIB|GMAB — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; ACORD data standards

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The primary regulatory framework governing this suitability review. NAIC_275 for annuity suitability; DOL_ERISA for employer-sponsored plan sales; SEC_FINRA for variable product sales; STATE_DOI for state-specific requirements; BEST_INTEREST for Reg BI compliance.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; DOL ERISA; SEC Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI); FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which required remediation actions must be completed. Populated when remediation_required_flag is True.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; State DOI market conduct examination standards

attributes.name: remediation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a compliance remediation action is required as a result of this suitability review, such as policy rescission, refund, or corrective disclosure.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; State DOI market conduct examination standards; SOX compliance

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the suitability review was conducted, corresponding to the point-of-sale (POS) transaction date.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; DOL ERISA fiduciary standards

attributes.name: review_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this suitability review at initiation, used for correspondence, audit trails, and regulatory filings. Format: SR-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation #275; FINRA Rule 2111

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the suitability review. 'suitable' indicates the product is appropriate for the client; 'not_suitable' triggers mandatory remediation; 'needs_review' requires supervisory escalation; 'escalated' indicates referral to compliance; 'withdrawn' indicates the transaction was cancelled.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; FINRA Rule 2111; DOL Fiduciary Rule

attributes.name: review_type
attributes.description: Classification of the review type. 'initial' for new sales; 'replacement' for policy replacements per NAIC Model #613; 'exchange' for 1035 tax-free exchanges; 'periodic' for ongoing best-interest reviews; 'supervisory' for principal-level reviews.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; NAIC Life Insurance Replacement Model Regulation #613; IRC Section 1035

attributes.name: risk_tolerance
attributes.description: Client's self-reported investment risk tolerance as captured on the suitability questionnaire. Determines appropriate product risk profile alignment.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6A; FINRA Rule 2111; SEC Regulation Best Interest

attributes.name: source_of_funds
attributes.description: The origin of the funds used to purchase the product. Required for AML/BSA compliance and suitability analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: savings|retirement_account|inheritance|proceeds_from_sale|existing_policy|business_income|gift|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FinCEN AML/BSA requirements; NAIC Model Regulation #275; ACORD data standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this suitability review record originated (e.g., CRM for Salesforce Financial Services Cloud, POLICY_ADMIN for Policy Administration System, COMPLIANCE_WB for compliance workbench).
attributes.references: ACORD data standards; internal data governance policy

attributes.name: suitability_determination
attributes.description: The formal suitability determination made by the reviewing agent: 'suitable' confirms the product meets the client's needs; 'not_suitable' prohibits the sale; 'conditionally_suitable' requires additional disclosures or client acknowledgment.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275 Section 6; DOL Fiduciary Rule; SEC Regulation Best Interest

attributes.name: supervisory_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the supervising principal documenting the basis for the supervisory review outcome, including any conditions, concerns, or required follow-up actions.

attributes.name: supervisory_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the supervisory or principal review of the suitability determination was completed.

attributes.name: supervisory_review_outcome
attributes.description: The outcome of the principal or supervisory compliance review of the suitability determination. 'approved' confirms the sale may proceed; 'rejected' halts the transaction; 'returned_for_revision' requires agent to update the analysis; 'escalated' refers to senior compliance.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation #275; FINRA Rule 3110 (Supervision); SEC Regulation Best Interest

attributes.name: tax_status
attributes.description: Tax qualification status of the funds used to purchase the product. 'qualified' indicates pre-tax retirement funds (IRA, 401k); 'non_qualified' indicates after-tax funds; 'roth' indicates Roth IRA funds. Affects IRC Section 72 tax treatment and suitability of tax-deferred products.
attributes.references: IRC Section 72; IRS Publication 575; DOL ERISA

attributes.name: variable_product_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the recommended product is a variable insurance or annuity product (e.g., VUL, variable annuity), triggering additional SEC/FINRA oversight, prospectus delivery, and suitability requirements.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 2111; SEC Regulation Best Interest

products.name: aml_case
products.description: Operational record of an Anti-Money Laundering (AML) or Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) investigation case initiated by automated transaction monitoring alerts or manual referrals. Captures case type (SAR, CTR, structuring, STOLI), subject policyholder or agent, triggering transaction details, case status (open, under review, filed, closed), assigned investigator, FinCEN filing reference, and disposition. Supports FinCEN SAR/CTR filing obligations and OFAC screening outcomes.

attributes.name: aml_case_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the AML/BSA investigation case record. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: agency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agent.agency. Business justification: AML investigations may reveal agency-level patterns: multiple producers within same agency involved in premium financing schemes, STOLI rings, or structured transactions. Agency context is critical fo

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: AML investigation programs have dedicated compliance cost centers. Investigation costs, external counsel fees, and FinCEN filing costs must be allocated to cost centers for BSA/AML program expense rep

attributes.name: insurance_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: AML cases require documented investigation evidence, transaction records, and narrative support for SAR filings. Essential for AML case management, FinCEN reporting, and regulatory examination defense

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: AML cases resulting in asset seizure, restitution payments, or regulatory penalties generate journal entries. Finance must track financial impact of AML cases for regulatory reporting and financial st

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.legal_entity. Business justification: AML cases are investigated and SAR filings made by specific legal entities. FinCEN filing requirement is entity-specific - each entity must have own AML program and file own SARs.

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the policyholder record associated with this AML/BSA case, when the subject is a policyholder or the suspicious activity is linked to a specific policy contract.
attributes.references: NAIC Life Insurance Model Regulation; Policy Administration System (Sapiens LifePro / FAST)

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.plan. Business justification: AML cases in life insurance are triggered by suspicious transactions on specific insurance plans (e.g., single-premium whole life used for structuring). FinCEN and ACLI guidance requires product-level

attributes.name: producer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed agent or broker associated with this AML/BSA case, when the subject or a contributing party is an agent. Used for producer conduct investigations and STOLI case tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act; Agent and Commission Management System (Sapiens Commission / Annocera); FinCEN SAR Form 111

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: AML/BSA cases are governed by specific regulatory obligations (BSA Section 314(a)/(b), FinCEN CDD Rule, OFAC compliance). Adding regulatory_obligation_id to aml_case normalizes the governing regulator

attributes.name: trade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.trade. Business justification: AML cases investigate suspicious trading activity (premium financing, STOLI indicators, rapid surrenders, unusual investment patterns). Real business process: suspicious activity investigation, SAR fi

attributes.name: activity_end_date
attributes.description: Latest date of the suspicious activity or transaction pattern under investigation. Together with activity_start_date, defines the full activity period reported on FinCEN SAR filings.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Activity Date Range; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: activity_start_date
attributes.description: Earliest date of the suspicious activity or transaction pattern under investigation. Used to define the activity period reported on FinCEN SAR filings and to scope the investigation lookback window.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Activity Date Range; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: case_closed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the AML/BSA investigation case was formally closed, either after FinCEN filing, no-filing determination, or referral to law enforcement. Null for open or in-progress cases.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the AML/BSA case, used in correspondence, FinCEN filings, and regulatory communications. Format: AML-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR/CTR Filing Requirements; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: case_opened_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the AML/BSA investigation case was formally opened and entered into the case management system. This is the principal business event timestamp for the case lifecycle and is used to calculate FinCEN filing deadline compliance (SAR must be filed within 30 days of detection).
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Filing Deadline 31 CFR Part 1020.320; BSA/AML Program Requirements

attributes.name: case_priority
attributes.description: Risk-based priority level assigned to the case, driving investigator workload management and escalation timelines. CRITICAL cases typically involve OFAC hits or law enforcement referrals.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle status of the AML/BSA investigation case. OPEN = newly initiated; UNDER_REVIEW = active investigation in progress; PENDING_FILING = investigation complete, awaiting FinCEN submission; FILED = SAR/CTR submitted to FinCEN; CLOSED = case resolved with no filing or post-filing closure; ESCALATED = referred to law enforcement or senior compliance.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; 31 CFR Part 1010.320; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: case_type
attributes.description: Classification of the AML/BSA investigation case by regulatory obligation or suspicious activity pattern. SAR = Suspicious Activity Report; CTR = Currency Transaction Report; STRUCTURING = deliberate transaction structuring to evade reporting thresholds; STOLI = Stranger-Originated Life Insurance fraud; OFAC = Office of Foreign Assets Control screening hit; KYC_REMEDIATION = Know Your Customer remediation case. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAR|CTR|STRUCTURING|STOLI|OFAC|KYC_REMEDIATION|OTHER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111; FinCEN CTR Form 112; BSA 31 CFR Part 1020; OFAC SDN List; NAIC STOLI Model Act

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this AML case record was first created in the compliance case management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per SOX controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; FinCEN Recordkeeping Requirements 31 CFR Part 1010.430

attributes.name: detection_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the suspicious activity or transaction was first detected or identified, which may precede the formal case opening date. Critical for calculating the 30-day SAR filing deadline from the date of initial detection per FinCEN requirements.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Filing Deadline 31 CFR Part 1020.320; FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual

attributes.name: disposition
attributes.description: Final or current disposition outcome of the AML/BSA investigation case. SAR_FILED = Suspicious Activity Report submitted to FinCEN; CTR_FILED = Currency Transaction Report submitted; NO_ACTION = investigation concluded with no suspicious activity confirmed; LAW_ENFORCEMENT_REFERRED = case escalated to law enforcement; POLICY_TERMINATED = associated policy cancelled due to AML findings; CLAIM_DENIED = associated claim denied due to AML findings; PENDING = disposition not yet determined. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAR_FILED|CTR_FILED|NO_ACTION|LAW_ENFORCEMENT_REFERRED|POLICY_TERMINATED|CLAIM_DENIED|PENDING — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: disposition_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative documenting the rationale for the case disposition, investigative findings summary, and any actions taken. Required for regulatory examination evidence and internal audit trail. Subject to SAR confidentiality provisions — must not be disclosed to the subject.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Confidentiality Provisions 31 CFR Part 1020.320(e); NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: fincen_filed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the SAR or CTR was successfully submitted to FinCEN via the BSA E-Filing System. Used to verify compliance with the 30-day (or 60-day) SAR filing deadline and for regulatory examination evidence.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Filing Deadline 31 CFR Part 1020.320; FinCEN BSA E-Filing System; BSA Compliance Program

attributes.name: fincen_filing_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) Filing Type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory report filed with FinCEN as a result of this AML/BSA case. SAR = Suspicious Activity Report (FinCEN Form 111); CTR = Currency Transaction Report (FinCEN Form 112); FBAR = Foreign Bank Account Report; NONE = case closed with no filing required after investigation.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111; FinCEN CTR Form 112; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010.311; 31 CFR Part 1010.320

attributes.name: fincen_reference_number
attributes.description: Confirmation reference number assigned by FinCEN upon successful submission of a SAR or CTR filing. Used to track filing status, respond to law enforcement requests, and demonstrate regulatory compliance. Null until filing is submitted and acknowledged.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA E-Filing System; 31 CFR Part 1010.320; FinCEN SAR Form 111

attributes.name: initiation_source
attributes.description: Origin channel that triggered the creation of this AML/BSA case. AUTOMATED_ALERT = transaction monitoring system rule fired; MANUAL_REFERRAL = compliance officer or business unit referral; LAW_ENFORCEMENT = subpoena or law enforcement request; REGULATORY_EXAM = identified during state DOI or FinCEN examination; INTERNAL_AUDIT = identified during SOX or internal audit review; AGENT_REFERRAL = agent or broker flagged suspicious activity.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; 31 CFR Part 1010.210; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: Two or three-letter code identifying the primary regulatory jurisdiction governing this AML case (e.g., US state code or federal jurisdiction code). Determines applicable state DOI reporting requirements and law enforcement referral protocols.
attributes.references: NAIC State Department of Insurance Regulations; FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; State AML Statutes

attributes.name: kyc_review_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Know Your Customer (KYC) Review Required Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this AML case has triggered a mandatory KYC enhanced due diligence (EDD) review for the subject policyholder or agent. True = KYC/EDD review required; False = standard KYC sufficient.
attributes.references: USA PATRIOT Act Section 326; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule 31 CFR Part 1010.230; FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp of the most recent modification to this AML case record. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for regulatory examination purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; FinCEN Recordkeeping Requirements 31 CFR Part 1010.430; NAIC Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: law_enforcement_agency
attributes.description: Name of the law enforcement agency to which this case was referred, if applicable (e.g., FBI, DEA, IRS-CI, State Attorney General). Null when law_enforcement_referral is False.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; USA PATRIOT Act; 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: law_enforcement_referral
attributes.description: Indicates whether this AML/BSA case has been referred to law enforcement agencies (e.g., FBI, DEA, IRS Criminal Investigation, state law enforcement). True = referral made; False = no referral.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; USA PATRIOT Act; 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: ofac_match_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or SDN entry name from the OFAC screening system when a potential or confirmed match is identified. Used for escalation documentation and regulatory reporting. Null when screening status is CLEAR or NOT_SCREENED.
attributes.references: OFAC SDN List; 31 CFR Part 501; FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements

attributes.name: ofac_screening_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Screening Status
attributes.description: Result of OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and sanctions list screening for the case subject. CONFIRMED_MATCH requires immediate case escalation and potential transaction blocking per OFAC compliance obligations.
attributes.references: OFAC SDN List Screening Requirements; 31 CFR Part 501; FinCEN BSA/AML Program Requirements; USA PATRIOT Act Section 326

attributes.name: risk_score
attributes.description: Quantitative risk score assigned to this AML case by the transaction monitoring system or compliance analyst, typically on a scale of 0-100. Higher scores indicate greater money laundering risk and drive case prioritization. Used for risk-based AML program management.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/AML Risk-Based Program Requirements; FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual; NAIC ERM Guidelines

attributes.name: sar_confidentiality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this case is subject to SAR confidentiality provisions under the BSA, prohibiting disclosure of the SAR filing or its existence to the subject of the report. True = SAR filed and confidentiality applies; False = no SAR filed or confidentiality not applicable.
attributes.references: BSA SAR Confidentiality 31 CFR Part 1020.320(e); USA PATRIOT Act Section 351; FinCEN Guidance FIN-2007-G003

attributes.name: sar_filing_deadline
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the SAR must be submitted to FinCEN, calculated as 30 days from the detection date (or 60 days if no subject is identified). Drives compliance SLA monitoring and escalation workflows.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Filing Deadline 31 CFR Part 1020.320; BSA Compliance Program Requirements

attributes.name: subject_date_of_birth
attributes.description: Date of birth of the individual subject under investigation, required for identity verification, OFAC screening, and FinCEN SAR filing. Null for entity (non-individual) subjects.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Subject Information; OFAC SDN Screening; KYC Requirements 31 CFR Part 1010.230

attributes.name: subject_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the primary individual or entity under investigation in this AML/BSA case, as reported on FinCEN SAR/CTR filings. Required for regulatory filing and OFAC screening.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Subject Information; FinCEN CTR Form 112; OFAC SDN Screening Requirements

attributes.name: subject_tax_number
attributes.description: Social Security Number (SSN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) / Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) of the AML case subject, used for FinCEN SAR/CTR filing and OFAC screening. Stored encrypted per HIPAA and IRS data security requirements.
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111; IRS TIN Requirements; 31 CFR Part 1010; HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR Part 164

attributes.name: subject_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary subject under investigation. Identifies whether the suspicious activity is associated with a policyholder, licensed agent/broker, policy beneficiary, unrelated third party, or a legal entity (trust, corporation).
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Subject Information; KYC/AML Program Requirements; NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act

attributes.name: suspicious_activity_type
attributes.description: Specific category of suspicious activity identified in the investigation, aligned with FinCEN SAR activity type classifications. Examples include: CASH_TRANSACTION, STRUCTURING, MONEY_LAUNDERING, FRAUD, TERRORIST_FINANCING, INSURANCE_FRAUD, STOLI, IDENTITY_THEFT, ELDER_FINANCIAL_ABUSE. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CASH_TRANSACTION|STRUCTURING|MONEY_LAUNDERING|FRAUD|TERRORIST_FINANCING|INSURANCE_FRAUD|STOLI|IDENTITY_THEFT|ELDER_FINANCIAL_ABUSE — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Suspicious Activity Classification; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010; NAIC STOLI Model Act

attributes.name: transaction_amount
attributes.description: Total dollar amount of the suspicious transaction(s) under investigation. For CTR cases, this is the cash transaction amount exceeding the $10,000 reporting threshold. For SAR cases, this is the aggregate amount of suspicious activity. Reported on FinCEN filings.
attributes.references: FinCEN CTR Threshold 31 CFR Part 1010.311; FinCEN SAR Form 111 — Amount Involved; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010

attributes.name: transaction_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the suspicious transaction amount. Typically USD for domestic cases; foreign currency cases may indicate additional money laundering risk.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FinCEN SAR Form 111; BSA 31 CFR Part 1010

products.name: privacy_incident
products.description: Record of a HIPAA privacy incident, data breach, or unauthorized disclosure of Protected Health Information (PHI) or Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Captures incident type, discovery date, affected individuals count, data elements exposed, breach determination (yes/no), notification obligations triggered (HHS, state AG, affected individuals), notification dates, and remediation actions taken. Supports HIPAA Breach Notification Rule compliance and state data breach law reporting.

attributes.name: privacy_incident_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the privacy incident record. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR §§ 164.400–414); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policy.in_force_policy. Business justification: Privacy incidents often involve specific policy records (e.g., unauthorized access, data breach). Linking enables tracking which policies were affected, supports breach notification requirements under

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.market_conduct_exam. Business justification: Privacy incidents may be identified during a market conduct examination (e.g., DOI examination of data handling practices). Adding market_conduct_exam_id to privacy_incident enables tracking of exam-i

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.template. Business justification: HIPAA and state breach notification laws require specific notification letter templates for affected individuals, HHS, and state AGs. Privacy incident response teams must track which approved notifica

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to underwriting.paramedical_exam. HIPAA requirement: breach notification for medical examination data. Link

attributes.description: Reference to the primary policyholder whose Protected Health Information (PHI) or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) was involved in the incident. Links to the policyholder master record.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.502); NAIC Model Privacy Act

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agent.producer. Business justification: Privacy incidents often involve producer actions: unauthorized PHI access, lost/stolen devices with customer data, email breaches. HIPAA breach investigations require tracking which producer caused or

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: HIPAA privacy incidents are governed by specific regulatory obligations (HIPAA Privacy Rule, HITECH Act, state breach notification laws). attributes.name: breach_determination_date

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.description: Format of the data involved in the privacy incident — electronic (digital files, databases, emails), paper (physical documents), verbal (oral disclosure), or mixed. Influences remediation approach and risk assessment scoring.

attributes.name: discovery_date

attributes.name: doi_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which notification was submitted to the State Department of Insurance. Under the NAIC model law, notification is generally required within 72 hours of determining a cybersecurity event.

attributes.name: doi_notification_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Department of Insurance (DOI) Notification Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether notification to the State Department of Insurance is required under the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law or state-specific insurance data security regulations.
attributes.references: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law § 5; State DOI Regulations

attributes.name: hhs_notification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) Notification Date
attributes.description: Date on which notification was submitted to HHS OCR via the breach reporting portal. Must occur within 60 days of discovery for breaches affecting 500+ individuals, or by March 1 of the following year for smaller breaches.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.408); HHS OCR Breach Reporting Portal

attributes.name: hhs_notification_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) Notification Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether notification to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights (HHS OCR) is required. True for all confirmed HIPAA breaches; breaches affecting 500+ individuals require immediate notification, others are reported annually.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.408); HHS OCR Breach Reporting Portal

attributes.name: incident_date
attributes.description: The date on which the privacy incident actually occurred or is estimated to have begun. May differ from discovery_date when incidents are discovered after the fact. Required for HHS OCR annual breach report.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.408); HHS OCR Breach Reporting Portal

attributes.name: incident_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the privacy incident — what happened, how it was discovered, what data was involved, and the circumstances of the unauthorized access or disclosure. Core documentation for regulatory submissions and internal investigations.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.408); HHS OCR Breach Reporting Portal; NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law

attributes.name: incident_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the privacy incident ceased or was contained. Used to calculate exposure duration and assess scope of harm for breach risk assessment.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.402); NIST SP 800-66 Rev. 2

attributes.name: incident_location
attributes.description: Physical or logical location where the privacy incident occurred (e.g., home office, branch office name, cloud environment, third-party vendor site). Used for root cause analysis and remediation targeting.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR § 164.310); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law § 4

attributes.name: incident_reference_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally referenceable identifier assigned to the privacy incident at intake (e.g., PI-2024-000123). Used in regulatory correspondence, HHS OCR submissions, and state AG notifications.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.408); HHS OCR Breach Reporting Portal

attributes.name: incident_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the privacy incident through its lifecycle — from initial intake through investigation, breach determination, notification, and closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|under_investigation|breach_confirmed|no_breach_determined|notified|closed|reopened — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.400); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law § 4

attributes.name: incident_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the privacy incident as defined by HHS OCR breach reporting categories. Drives notification obligations and remediation workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: unauthorized_access|unauthorized_disclosure|lost_device|stolen_device|hacking_it_incident|improper_disposal|mailing_error|other — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: includes_financial_account
attributes.description: Indicates whether financial account numbers, payment card data, or banking information were among the data elements exposed. Triggers PCI DSS notification obligations and heightened state breach law requirements.
attributes.references: State Data Breach Notification Laws; PCI DSS v4.0; GLBA Safeguards Rule (16 CFR Part 314)

attributes.name: includes_health_information
attributes.description: Indicates whether Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined under HIPAA was among the data elements exposed. Determines applicability of HIPAA Breach Notification Rule and state health privacy laws.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.501); HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.400)

attributes.name: includes_ssn
attributes.description: Indicates whether Social Security Numbers (SSNs) were among the data elements exposed in the incident. SSN exposure triggers mandatory notification under virtually all 50 state data breach notification laws and heightens identity theft risk assessment.
attributes.references: State Data Breach Notification Laws (all 50 states); FinCEN AML/BSA; IRS TIN regulations

attributes.name: individual_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which written notification was sent to affected individuals. Must occur within 60 days of discovery of a confirmed breach. Supports HIPAA compliance deadline tracking.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.404(b)); HHS OCR Guidance

attributes.name: individual_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether written notification to affected individuals is required under the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule. Required for all confirmed breaches; must be sent within 60 days of discovery.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.404); HHS OCR Guidance

attributes.name: involved_business_associate
attributes.description: Indicates whether a HIPAA Business Associate (BA) — such as a TPA, vendor, or service provider — was involved in or responsible for the privacy incident. Business associates have independent HIPAA breach notification obligations to the covered entity.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.502(e)); HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.410)

attributes.name: is_breach_determined
attributes.description: Indicates whether the privacy incident has been formally determined to constitute a reportable breach under the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule following completion of the four-factor risk assessment. True = breach confirmed; False = not a breach (low probability of compromise).
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.402); HHS OCR Guidance on Breach Determination

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code of the primary jurisdiction governing notification obligations for this incident. Determines which state data breach notification law applies and the applicable notification deadline.
attributes.references: State Data Breach Notification Laws (all 50 states + DC); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp of the most recent modification to the privacy incident record. Supports audit trail integrity and change management tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR § 164.312(b))

attributes.name: media_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which notification was provided to prominent media outlets in the affected state(s). Required within 60 days of discovery for breaches affecting 500+ residents of a state.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.406(b)); HHS OCR Guidance

attributes.name: media_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether notification to prominent media outlets is required. Triggered when a confirmed breach affects 500 or more residents of a single state or jurisdiction.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.406); HHS OCR Guidance

attributes.name: multi_state_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the incident involves affected individuals across multiple states, triggering notification obligations under multiple state data breach notification laws simultaneously.
attributes.references: State Data Breach Notification Laws (all 50 states); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law

attributes.name: no_breach_rationale
attributes.description: Documented justification when the incident is determined NOT to constitute a reportable breach, referencing the four-factor risk assessment outcome (nature/extent of PHI, unauthorized person, whether PHI was actually acquired/viewed, extent of risk mitigation). Required for HIPAA documentation obligations.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.402(2)); HHS OCR Guidance

attributes.name: notification_deadline_date
attributes.description: Calculated deadline by which all required notifications (HHS OCR, individuals, media, state AG, DOI) must be completed. Derived from discovery_date plus the applicable regulatory notification window (e.g., 60 days under HIPAA, 30–72 hours under NAIC model law). Stored for deadline monitoring and escalation.
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.404–408); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law § 5; State Data Breach Notification Laws

attributes.name: phi_data_elements_exposed
attributes.business_glossary_term: Protected Health Information (PHI) Data Elements Exposed
attributes.description: Comma-delimited list of PHI or PII data element categories involved in the incident (e.g., name, SSN, date_of_birth, diagnosis, policy_number, financial_account, biometric). Required for HHS OCR breach report and state AG notifications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: name|ssn|date_of_birth|diagnosis|treatment|policy_number|financial_account|biometric|address|email|phone — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.408(b)(1)); HHS OCR Breach Reporting Portal

attributes.name: remediation_actions_taken
attributes.description: Narrative description of corrective and remediation actions taken in response to the privacy incident (e.g., system access revoked, encryption implemented, workforce retrained, BA agreement updated, policy revised). Required for HIPAA documentation and regulatory examination.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.530(i)); HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR § 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law § 4

attributes.name: remediation_completed_date
attributes.description: Date on which all remediation actions were confirmed as completed. Supports closure of the incident record and regulatory documentation of corrective action.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.530(i)); SOX Section 302; NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which all remediation actions must be completed. Used for compliance tracking and escalation management.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.530(i)); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law § 4

attributes.name: reported_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time the privacy incident was formally reported to the compliance or privacy office. Establishes the internal reporting timeline for SOX controls and HIPAA workforce training obligations.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR § 164.530(j)); SOX Section 302/906

attributes.name: risk_assessment_score
attributes.description: Overall risk level determined by the four-factor HIPAA breach risk assessment: (1) nature and extent of PHI involved, (2) identity of unauthorized person, (3) whether PHI was actually acquired or viewed, (4) extent to which risk has been mitigated. attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level categorization of the root cause of the privacy incident. Used for trend analysis, remediation prioritization, and regulatory reporting to HHS OCR and state DOIs. attributes.references: NIST SP 800-66 Rev. 2; HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR § 164.308(a)(1)); NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law

attributes.name: state_ag_notification_date

attributes.name: state_ag_notification_required

attributes.description: Indicates whether notification to the State Attorney General is required under applicable state data breach notification law. Requirements vary by state.

products.name: policy_form_approval
products.description: Master record of state DOI filings for policy forms, rider forms, endorsement forms, and premium rate schedules. For form filings: captures form number, form type (base policy, rider, endorsement, application), product line, filing method (prior approval, file-and-use, use-and-file), state, submission/approval dates, approval reference, and form status. For rate filings: captures filing type (new rate, rate revision, LTC rate increase), actuarial justification reference, proposed effective date, approval status, rate change percentage, and DOI response details. Ensures only approved forms and rates are used in each jurisdiction, supports state rate regulation compliance, and serves as the single source of truth for all form and rate approval status across all jurisdictions.
